summary: Ecosystem food supply services are the foundation of sustainable development of society and nature. Taking the Chongqing main city as an example, based on multi-source data such as land use, food production and population, the supply and de
content: Ecosystem food supply services are the foundation of sustainable development of society and nature. Taking the Chongqing main city as an example, based on multi-source data such as land use, food production and population, the supply and demand of food supply services (FS) were quantified by food calorie method. Then, the supply and demand relationships were clarified based on the supply-demand ratio and bivariate local spatial autocorrelation. Finally, the spatial flow characteristics of FS were explored based on transportation accessibility. The results show that: (1) From 2000 to 2020, the FS supply decreased from 5.2 × 10 12 to 1.7 × 10 12 kcal, and the high-supply areas disappeared in the west and only remained in the northeast and southeast. The FS demand increased from 4.7 × 10 10 to 6.5 × 10 10 kcal, and the high-demand areas expanded from the middle to the east and west sides. (2) The average supply-demand ratio of FS decreased from 0.348 to 0.222, indicating an increase in supply pressure. The area of the surplus regions shrank while that of the deficit regions expanded. In particular, the areas with high demand and low supply were significantly increased. (3) The spatial flow of FS was mainly concentrated in two directions: from Banan to the central and southern demand areas and from Yubei to the northern demand areas. The research results can provide strong data support for optimizing regional food resource allocation and promoting regional sustainable development.

title: Second-crop corn in the State of Paraná
summary: The second-crop corn has become one of the main agricultural production systems in Brazil, with the state of Paraná being one of the largest national producers of this crop. The expansion of the soybean-corn system has significantly contrib
content: The second-crop corn has become one of the main agricultural production systems in Brazil, with the state of Paraná being one of the largest national producers of this crop. The expansion of the soybean-corn system has significantly contributed to increased grain production and the strengthening of animal protein production chains, playing a strategic role in the state and national economy. However, second-crop corn cultivation is subject to several factors that limit productivity, notably abiotic stresses such as water deficit, low temperatures, frosts, and irregular rainfall distribution, as well as biotic factors such as the corn leafhopper (Dalbulus maidis), the corn stunt complex, foliar diseases, insect pests, and weeds. These factors directly affect the physiological and biochemical processes of the plant, compromising the growth, development, and yield of cultivated hybrids. In this context, genetic improvement plays a fundamental role in the development of cultivars better adapted to the edaphoclimatic conditions of Paraná. The use of modern tools, such as marker-assisted selection, genomic selection, high-precision phenotyping, digital agriculture, remote sensing, and gene editing, has contributed to accelerating the development of more productive, resistant, and stable hybrids. Furthermore, the integration of breeding technologies, agronomic management, and climate monitoring represents a promising strategy to minimize the impacts of climate change and increase the sustainability of the production system. Therefore, this review gathers and discusses the main aspects related to the cultivation of second-crop maize in the state of Paraná, addressing the factors that influence productivity, the physiological and genetic mechanisms of resistance, the technological advances applied to genetic improvement, and the prospects for the development of more resilient and efficient production systems.

title: Engineering biofilm growth regimes in FDM-printed plastics through material selection
summary: Biofilm formation on 3D-printed surfaces presents either a challenge to mitigate or an opportunity to exploit. While medical and industrial applications require suppressing microbial colonization, biofilm-based biotechnologies rely on rapid
content: Biofilm formation on 3D-printed surfaces presents either a challenge to mitigate or an opportunity to exploit. While medical and industrial applications require suppressing microbial colonization, biofilm-based biotechnologies rely on rapid, stable establishment. Here, we demonstrate that FDM-printed plastics define tunable regimes of early biofilm formation through material selection. Ten polymers and composites, including PLA+, ABS, PC+, and glass-fiber reinforced variants, were evaluated against six microbial strains. SEM (Scanning Electron Microscopy) and machine-learning-assisted image analysis revealed distinct colonization patterns, ranging from minimal attachment to matrix-rich coverage. PA, PC+, and ABS/PA-GF8 were highly biofilm-prone, while HIPS, PP, and TPU showed significantly lower susceptibility. Surface topography and glass-fiber reinforcement were identified as key drivers of these differences. These results establish a framework for engineering biofilm growth on FDM plastics, enabling precise material selection to either suppress or promote colonization. These findings provide design guidance for additive manufacturing in biofouling-sensitive and biofilm-enabled applications.

title: Beyond green: Unveiling the drivers of gross ecosystem product in high-density urban green spaces — A case study of central Beijing
summary: Rapid population growth and intensive urbanization continue to threaten the supply of ecosystem services (ES) in cities. In high-density urban areas, the planning and management of urban green spaces (UGS) under complex landuse constraints
content: Rapid population growth and intensive urbanization continue to threaten the supply of ecosystem services (ES) in cities. In high-density urban areas, the planning and management of urban green spaces (UGS) under complex landuse constraints are vital for sustainable urban renewal. Gross ecosystem product (GEP) provides a practical framework for valuing ES and guiding sustainability policies. However, UGS are often fragmented by buildings and roads into isolated ecological units, while existing studies remain largely at macro or administrative scales, overlooking patch-scale GEP variations. As a bridge between internal ecological processes and urban spatial patterns, the patch scale is essential for refined and comparable GEP accounting. This study developed a patch-scale framework to enhance the ecological value of UGS in dense cities. By integrating multisource semantic data, an object-based approach, and random forest modeling, we quantified GEP and identified the driving mechanisms across UGS types in central Beijing. In 2023, total GEP reached 160.86 billion CNY, averaging 143.27 CNY/m²; parks showed the highest values, followed by subsidiary and other green spaces. The magnitude and direction of influencing factors varied across UGS types: management dominated GEP in parks, while vegetation features played major roles in subsidiary and other green spaces. The variables year and greenspace components exhibited opposite marginal effects between parks and the other two types. This study highlights the patch scale as the smallest unit for policy implementation and spatial regulation, providing quantitative and managerial insights for optimizing green spaces and advancing standardized, comparable urban ecosystem service assessments.

title: Pickering emulsions: emulsion polymerization and systems stabilized with carbon allotropes or carbon-rich materials
summary: The use of Pickering emulsions (PEs) has recently expanded considerably in academia and industry due to their ease of preparation, remarkable stability, and versatility in applications. This review focuses on PEs stabilized by carbon-rich p
content: The use of Pickering emulsions (PEs) has recently expanded considerably in academia and industry due to their ease of preparation, remarkable stability, and versatility in applications. This review focuses on PEs stabilized by carbon-rich particles, such as functionalized graphene and graphene oxide (GO), among others. It includes general PE production and applications along with the stabilization of emulsions in which an emulsion polymerization occurs to generate a polymer that plays a key role in the final application. Novel aspects of this study compared to others consist of its focus on carbon-rich stabilizers and its inclusion of emulsion polymerization applications. The key factor to obtain a stable PE with these materials is to guarantee that they exhibit an amphiphilic nature (which is tunable in many cases) to stabilize the emulsion. The majority of the applications in recent literature use GO as a PE stabilizer due to its inherent amphiphilicity and versatility for further chemical modification. The most significant challenge for final applications is the scaling up of the production process of GO or other carbon-based materials as stabilizers so that they can perform reproducibly as PE stabilizers, as these processes are subject to significant variability. Future research will diversify and consolidate applications, focusing more on the practical implementation of these developments involving aspects such as scaling up, efficiency, and recyclability.

title: Integrating traditional forestry and modern carbon markets: a systematic review of silviculture, geospatial technologies, and jurisdictional REDD+ in the climate change era
summary: Climate change presents urgent challenges for forests but also creates new opportunities through carbon markets. This systematic review, conducted according to PRISMA guidelines, synthesizes 60 studies across four themes: climate change imp
content: Climate change presents urgent challenges for forests but also creates new opportunities through carbon markets. This systematic review, conducted according to PRISMA guidelines, synthesizes 60 studies across four themes: climate change impacts, forest management and technologies, carbon market dynamics, and jurisdictional REDD+ (J-REDD+). The findings indicate that climate impacts are already severe: rising temperatures have increased forest mortality, disturbance frequency, and carbon sink degradation. Advances in geospatial technologies including remote sensing, LiDAR, unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), and artificial intelligence (AI), now enable accurate, cost-effective, and near-real-time forest carbon monitoring, supporting jurisdictional accounting. Carbon markets are evolving rapidly, demand for high-integrity credits is projected to exceed supply in near future, creating significant opportunities for forest-rich developing countries. J-REDD+ under ART TREES marks a paradigm shift by addressing systematic leakage, permanence, and over-crediting. The study underscores the importance of early readiness, governance reform, technological capacity, and strategic investment to achieve resilient and equitable forest outcomes.

title: Genotypic Variation and the Effects of Nitric Oxide and 1-Methylcyclopropene on Mitigating Blackspot Bruise Enzymatic Browning in Potatoes
summary: Abstract Blackspot bruise is a common defect caused by physical injury of potato tubers that triggers internal enzymatic browning, leading to significant postharvest losses. Reducing the development of internal discolouration has enormous b
content: Abstract Blackspot bruise is a common defect caused by physical injury of potato tubers that triggers internal enzymatic browning, leading to significant postharvest losses. Reducing the development of internal discolouration has enormous benefits for the industry. The objective of this study was to evaluate the efficacy of nitric oxide (NO) and 1-methylcyclopropene (1-MCP) in controlling blackspot enzymatic browning in Clearwater Russet, Russet Burbank, and Russet Norkotah potato cultivars. Tubers from these three cultivars were treated with NO (98 mL L −1 ; 5 h) and 1-MCP (0.139 mL L −1 ; 24 h), in addition to the untreated control. After the application of these treatments, half of the tubers were stored at 7.2 °C and 95% relative humidity (RH) for 14 days. The remaining half of the tubers were injured to induce blackspot bruising and then held for 24 h at 23 °C and 65% RH to allow browning symptoms to develop. 1-MCP and NO treatments significantly reduced blackspot enzymatic browning score to 1.3 and 1.1, respectively, compared to the untreated control (1.8) on a scale from 1 (lightest) to 4 (darkest). Treated tubers maintained higher lightness (L*) value of bruise area after peeling 70.47 in 1-MCP and 69.35 in NO, compared to the control, 66.67. Biochemical profile does not show any significant changes with treatment. This study provides preliminary proof of approaches to minimise bruise-associated discolouration in potatoes, with the potential to reduce postharvest losses and enhance the marketable value of fresh potatoes, which needs further verification to see its further implications.

title: The combined effects of the EU carbon border adjustment mechanism and the EU deforestation regulation on ASEAN wood exports: a simulation analysis using the GTAP-E model
summary: The EU Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) and the EU Deforestation Regulation (EUDR) are key instruments of the European Union’s green trade policy. This study employs the GTAP-E (Global Trade Analysis Project–Energy) model to assess
content: The EU Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) and the EU Deforestation Regulation (EUDR) are key instruments of the European Union’s green trade policy. This study employs the GTAP-E (Global Trade Analysis Project–Energy) model to assess their impacts on wood exports from the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN). The results indicate that CBAM has a relatively moderate effect, operating mainly through indirect cost transmission channels. In contrast, EUDR significantly constrains exports, output, and welfare by increasing compliance costs and tightening market access requirements. Under the combined scenario, the two policies generate an amplification effect, further intensifying trade contraction. Indonesia, Malaysia and Vietnam are the most adversely affected, while countries such as Singapore exhibit a certain degree of resilience. Overall, green trade policies may exacerbate existing development imbalances. In response, it is recommended that the EU strengthen support for technology transfer and capacity building, while ASEAN countries should enhance forest governance and promote export market diversification.

title: Thinking big in small scale: characterization of peroxidase production in Komagataella phaffii using two-compartment scale-down system
summary: Abstract The replacement of cobalt-based siccatives in unsaturated polyester resin curing requires sustainable and scalable biocatalytic alternatives, with fungal peroxidases representing a promising option. For industrial implementation, h
content: Abstract The replacement of cobalt-based siccatives in unsaturated polyester resin curing requires sustainable and scalable biocatalytic alternatives, with fungal peroxidases representing a promising option. For industrial implementation, however, robust large-scale production processes are essential. In this study, we investigated the robustness of a glycerol-based peroxidase production process in K. phaffii driven by the glycerol-derepressible P DF promoter, focusing on industrially relevant bioreactor inhomogeneities. A two-compartment scale-down system was used to mimic substrate and oxygen gradients arising from insufficient mixing and mass transfer at large scale. Substrate inhomogeneity alone led to a moderate reduction in peroxidase titers (approx. 23%), indicating partial sensitivity to localized substrate oversupply. In contrast, simultaneous substrate and oxygen inhomogeneity resulted in a counterintuitive increase in peroxidase titers of approx. 13% compared to homogeneous reference conditions. This suggests that dynamic transitions between substrate limitation and surplus can positively affect peroxidase formation under P DF promoter control. Based on this observation, a modified process strategy incorporating glycerol pulses during the depression phase was evaluated. While this approach demonstrated high robustness, it did not enhance productivity. Overall, the results demonstrate that the developed K. phaffii process is resilient to large-scale inhomogeneities and can even benefit from specific dynamic cultivation conditions.

title: How to Evaluate the Relevance of Skills and Competencies
summary: This chapter discusses the rationale and means to evaluate the relevance of transferable competencies and skills for engineering degrees. It presents three processes that have been used in different contexts to identify which transferable s
content: This chapter discusses the rationale and means to evaluate the relevance of transferable competencies and skills for engineering degrees. It presents three processes that have been used in different contexts to identify which transferable skills and competencies are needed in engineering work. The cases also illustrate how the viewpoints of different stakeholders can be brought to the table. Although the evaluation of the relevance of skills may be more pertinent to programme heads and other educational leaders responsible for the construction of entire degrees, knowing about these processes and their outcomes can also benefit lecturers of a single course or module by showing where some of the requirements set for the teachers originate from and how they are justified. The chapter finishes with recommendations for those who wish to conduct an evaluation of relevance in their own context.

title: Innovative Fabrication of Advanced Robots Using the WASPAS Method: A New Era in Robotics Engineering
summary: The fabrication of advanced robots represents a pivotal intersection of cutting-edge materials science, artificial intelligence, and innovative manufacturing techniques. However, the rise of these machines also raises important questions ab
content: The fabrication of advanced robots represents a pivotal intersection of cutting-edge materials science, artificial intelligence, and innovative manufacturing techniques. However, the rise of these machines also raises important questions about societal impacts, ethical considerations, and job displacement. The ongoing advancements in robot fabrication promise to reshape industries and redefine the role of automation in human life. The significance of research in the fabrication of advanced robots lies in its trans formative potential across numerous sectors. Furthermore, it tackles ethical, social, and economic implications, guiding responsible innovation to ensure positive societal impact while mitigating job displacement and other risks. The fabrication of advanced robots involves a multi-disciplinary methodology combining materials science, manufacturing techniques, and artificial intelligence (AI). The process starts with designing robot structures using lightweight, durable materials like composites and metals. Additive manufacturing (3D printing) and precision machining are employed to create complex components. Sensors, actuators, and processors are integrated to enable movement and functionality. AI and machine learning models are embedded for autonomous decision-making, adapting robot behaviors to dynamic environments. Testing and iterative prototyping ensure performance, reliability, and safety. Finally, robots undergo optimization for energy efficiency, user interaction, and task-specific capabilities in their intended applications. R-Alpha, R-Beta, R-Gamma, R-Delta, R-Epsilon. Precision (B1), Speed (B2), Durability (B3), Energy Efficiency (B4). R-Alpha is getting first place of the table and R-Delta is getting last place of the table

title: Balancing biodiversity and profitability: pathways to sustainable robusta coffee production in Vietnam’s central highlands
summary: Coffee production in Vietnam’s Central Highlands is important for rural livelihoods and national export earnings, but the sector faces growing pressure from climate variability, declining soil fertility, and biodiversity loss. Intercropping
content: Coffee production in Vietnam’s Central Highlands is important for rural livelihoods and national export earnings, but the sector faces growing pressure from climate variability, declining soil fertility, and biodiversity loss. Intercropping and adjustments in planting density are increasingly promoted as part of diversified coffee-production systems, although their relationships with productivity and farm revenue remain insufficiently understood. This study examined how these management practices were associated with coffee yield, coffee gross revenue, non-coffee gross revenue, and total gross farm revenue in robusta coffee systems. The analysis used 332 farm-year observations from 83 farms in Gia Lai and Lam Dong provinces, collected over four consecutive coffee crop years: 2021–22, 2022–23, 2023–24, and 2024–25. A management-based Biodiversity Practice Index was developed using cropping system and coffee planting density. Farms were classified as Low, Moderate, or High BPI. Descriptive comparisons and adjusted regression models with farm-clustered robust standard errors were used to assess differences across management systems. Low BPI and sole-coffee farms generally recorded the highest coffee yield and coffee gross revenue. Moderate BPI farms recorded the highest total gross farm revenue because revenue from intercrops partly offset lower coffee-derived revenue. After separating coffee and non-coffee revenue, the results did not show a clear BPI advantage for coffee gross revenue alone. Overall, the findings indicate a trade-off between coffee-specialised production and revenue diversification. Intercropping broadened farm revenue sources, but the study does not provide direct evidence of improved ecological biodiversity, sustainability, profitability, or resilience.

title: Public health, trade unions and empowerment: From learning to draft resolutions to addressing the socioeconomic determinants of health
summary: Abstract Community empowerment projects aimed at improving health and wellbeing have tended to be ‘place-based’. But they may also be based on ‘communities of interest’. This paper advances an original conception of health-related empowerme
content: Abstract Community empowerment projects aimed at improving health and wellbeing have tended to be ‘place-based’. But they may also be based on ‘communities of interest’. This paper advances an original conception of health-related empowerment by focusing on the work of trade unions, which we treat as being among such communities. Organised labour improves health and reduces inequalities through processes including collective bargaining, even as public health actors have shown resistance to engaging with unions. We focus on an unresearched area of unions’ andragogy that is central to empowerment: that of motion writing and resolution-related mobilisation, arguing this has direct and underexploited implications for public health. Drawing on triangulated data from a UK-wide survey of unions representing more than 2 million members, in-depth interviews and website analysis, we consider how resolution-associated practices can form bridges between people’s individual concerns and collective decision-making. Such ‘micro-meso-macro’ connections can support initiatives that other empowerment projects have failed to establish. This generates a new resolutions-based conceptual model: the multi-level empowerment pathway. Our research contests the prevailing public health paradigm. We build on previous union–health research to help reconsider action on health determinants operating as global challenges, suggesting an internationally applicable infrastructure for participatory action.

title: Dataset for "External Rating Coverage in the Voluntary Carbon Market"
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: This dataset contains project-level data used in the empirical analysis of the study “External Rating Coverage in the Voluntary Carbon Market”. The dataset combines information on voluntary carbon market projects registered under the Verra
content: This dataset contains project-level data used in the empirical analysis of the study “External Rating Coverage in the Voluntary Carbon Market”. The dataset combines information on voluntary carbon market projects registered under the Verra Verified Carbon Standard (VCS) with external rating information from BeZero Carbon. It includes project identifiers, project names, host countries, project types, BeZero registry identifiers, assessment status, external ratings, rating dates, corresponding BeZero URLs, and an indicator identifying whether a Verra project was matched with a BeZero record. The dataset was compiled and processed by the authors for descriptive analysis and logistic regression examining the determinants of external rating coverage.

title: Spatial association and convergence of the water–energy–food nexus in the Yellow River Basin using a graph-convolution-assisted spatial econometric model
summary: Water, energy, and food security are jointly constrained by ecological pressure, resource scarcity, and uneven regional development in the Yellow River Basin. This study examines the spatial association and convergence of the water–energy–f
content: Water, energy, and food security are jointly constrained by ecological pressure, resource scarcity, and uneven regional development in the Yellow River Basin. This study examines the spatial association and convergence of the water–energy–food nexus across nine provincial regions from 2011 to 2021. A composite development index is constructed by combining CRITIC and entropy weights. Geographical proximity and pairwise dependence between provincial WEF index series are then integrated into an equally weighted hybrid spatial matrix. Graph convolution is used as a transparent neighborhood aggregation step that transforms standardized regional covariates before they enter a spatial Durbin specification and a spatial absolute beta-convergence model. Global Moran’s I increases from 0.235 to 0.318, indicating persistent and strengthening positive spatial dependence. The reported point estimates show that indirect effects account for 30.4% to 31.3% of the total effects of the examined factors. The basin-wide beta coefficient is negative 0.423 and the spatial lag coefficient is positive 0.286, which is consistent with faster growth in regions with lower initial WEF development and with positive neighborhood association. Three development-profile groups display different initial levels and adjustment speeds. These groups are interpreted as exploratory regional profiles rather than formal Phillips-Sul convergence clubs. The findings support basin-wide coordination while also showing that policy design should reflect differences in resource endowment, internal variation, and regional development stage.

title: Imaginative reuse of concrete: Material afterlives, sustainability, and urban memory in Ankara’s 100th Anniversary Mall
summary: This study examines the demolition of a 1970s public building on a historically layered site in Ankara and its transformation into an urban park. The structure was fractured for steel recovery, while concrete waste was discarded, eliminatin
content: This study examines the demolition of a 1970s public building on a historically layered site in Ankara and its transformation into an urban park. The structure was fractured for steel recovery, while concrete waste was discarded, eliminating material and architectural traces. This loss reflects a recurring pattern of spatial erasure across the site’s history. The research proposes an alternative approach that reuses the discarded concrete in situ to preserve and reinterpret traces within the new park. The methodology combines historical analysis, documentation of the demolition, and laboratory testing of concrete to assess material performance. Spatial parameters are identified, their reinterpretations are integrated, and their compatibility with current programmatic needs and material capacities is evaluated. The approach is demonstrated through a design proposal that communicates historical transformations, demolition sequence, and material reuse to the public. Findings are distilled into three transferable design questions for historically significant contexts where demolition is unavoidable.

title: GDP, Growth, and Welfare
summary: In the years following World War II, the main economic goal of countries, and the main standard by which economies were judged, was the performance of their Gross Domestic Product (GDP), which was defined and measured following rules create
content: In the years following World War II, the main economic goal of countries, and the main standard by which economies were judged, was the performance of their Gross Domestic Product (GDP), which was defined and measured following rules created by statisticians and economists who had developed the official national accounts statistics, mostly in the 1930s. The pursuit of the growth of the GDP has remained an overwhelming objective for most economists, politicians, and international organizations. GDP, Growth, and Welfare: In Pursuit of Economic Wellbeing examines several concepts and processes related to economic growth such as environmental degradation and climate change; income distribution and poverty; a vibrant civil society; and personal happiness. The text tackles the important question of whether growth itself can create problems that reduce its welfare value to populations. It weaves together two stories: the first concerns the invention of a statistical index, while the second explores the set of phenomena to which it applies. The author argues that reducing our dedication to economic growth should not be interpreted as stunting the growth of countries’ GDPs at their current level, but rather as focusing on paying more attention to the factors that may reduce the social benefits of this growth. The book addresses an important topic that has recently been an object of study in multiple fields such as economics, history, and ecology. It combines historical, analytical, and policy-oriented approaches into a single study and will attract the attention of scholars, researchers, economists, political scientists, and philosophers at a time when many traditional policies are being questioned and are under discussion.

title: Fishery facilities construction and fishers' income: evidence from China
summary: Introduction Increasing fishers' income is central to achieving sustainable fisheries development, while fishery facilities construction, as a form of social overhead capital, ensures the efficient operation of the entire fisheries industry
content: Introduction Increasing fishers' income is central to achieving sustainable fisheries development, while fishery facilities construction, as a form of social overhead capital, ensures the efficient operation of the entire fisheries industry chain. This study aims to examine the relationship between fishery facilities construction and fishers' income. Methods Based on panel data from 30 Chinese provinces over the period 2000–2024, this study first applies the entropy-weighted TOPSIS method to comprehensively assess the level of fishery facilities construction. Fixed-effects and mediation models are then employed to empirically examine the relationship between fishery facilities construction and fishers' income. Results The results show a positive relationship between fishery facilities construction and fishers' income, and this finding remains robust after a series of robustness and endogeneity tests. Regarding potential mediating channels, fishery scientific and technological innovation, aquatic product output, and fishery industrial agglomeration each exhibit a positive mediating relationship between fishery facilities construction and fishers' income. These three mediators also show sequential and interaction-based mediating relationships. In addition, fishery productivity and fishery disaster intensity provide evidence of alternative mediating mechanisms. Furthermore, the positive relationship between fishery facilities construction and fishers' income is more pronounced in economically developed regions, coastal regions, and regions where fishers have stronger technical capabilities. Discussion The findings of this study not only enrich the theoretical literature on fishery facilities and fishers' income but also provide important insights for the strategic decision-making of governments and fishers. Nevertheless, this study has several limitations, including the lack of sufficiently disaggregated micro-level data and the difficulty of completely eliminating potential endogeneity concerns.

title: Quantum Topological Autonomous Decision Ecosystems for Geoeconomic Risk, Climate, Energy Markets, Smart Cities and Resilient Global Infrastructure
source: International Journal of Academic and Industrial Research Innovations(IJAIRI)
summary: Abstract: Contemporary geoeconomic fragmentation, climate-transition pressures, volatile energy markets, digitally interconnected cities and increasingly interdependent infrastructure systems generate systemic risks that cannot be adequatel
content: Abstract: Contemporary geoeconomic fragmentation, climate-transition pressures, volatile energy markets, digitally interconnected cities and increasingly interdependent infrastructure systems generate systemic risks that cannot be adequately represented through isolated sectoral models. This paper develops an integrated Quantum-Topological Autonomous Decision Ecosystem for Global Resilience (Q-TADER-GR) to represent, forecast and manage multidomain risk propagation across geoeconomic, climate-financial, energy, urban and infrastructure networks. The study adopts a model-based analytical research design combining multiplex graph theory, topological data analysis, dynamic systems modelling, probabilistic risk forecasting, autonomous decision optimisation and a conceptual quantum-computational layer. Persistent topological features are used to identify structural dependencies and regime transitions that conventional pairwise indicators may overlook, while autonomous controls are formulated as constrained optimisation interventions. Quantum algorithms are positioned as potential computational accelerators for persistence calculations and high-dimensional optimisation rather than as assumptions that socioeconomic processes themselves are quantum mechanical. An illustrative 0-10 numerical application generates a baseline weighted sectoral risk of 6.85 and a topology-adjusted systemic risk of approximately 6.87. Under a hypothetical coordinated intervention scenario, adjusted systemic risk declines to approximately 5.71 while the proposed Net Resilience Readiness Index improves from 5.06 to 5.69, representing an illustrative improvement of approximately 12.6%. These values are demonstrative rather than empirical. The principal contribution is a unified analytical architecture capable of connecting systemic-risk detection, climate-finance integrity, electricity-market stability, smart-city digital twins, cross-sector infrastructure resilience and autonomous policy decision support within a common mathematically interpretable framework. Keywords: quantum topological data analysis; autonomous decision intelligence; geoeconomic fragmentation; systemic risk; climate finance; carbon transition risk; energy-market resilience; smart cities; urban digital twins; infrastructure resilience; persistent homology; multiplex networks; quantum optimisation; systemic contagion; policy intelligence

title: Uniaxial variable-stiffness layup configuration for carbon fiber-reinforced polymer laminates to improve bending performance
summary: Curved fiber tows offer a promising alternative to classical constant stiffness composites in terms of design and performance. However, the analysis of such structures is more challenging because the fiber orientation and the resulting stif
content: Curved fiber tows offer a promising alternative to classical constant stiffness composites in terms of design and performance. However, the analysis of such structures is more challenging because the fiber orientation and the resulting stiffness properties vary continuously over the laminate. In this study, a uniaxial variable-stiffness layup configuration is proposed, in which “uniaxial” means that the fiber orientation and the resulting stiffness distribution vary only along a single in-plane coordinate direction, namely the x -axis, rather than over the general two-dimensional x – y domain. This design incorporates a specific strategy for planning the curved trajectories of the fiber tows. For the bending analysis of the resulting uniaxial variable-stiffness laminates, a finite strip formulation is adapted to account for the spatially varying stiffness coefficients. Furthermore, a response-surface proxy model based on the radial basis function is constructed to establish the relationship between design variables and laminate center deflection. Comparison with experimental results demonstrates that the designed uniaxial variable-stiffness laminates effectively facilitate load transfer, mitigating stress concentration and delaying damage initiation.

title: Is China's urban green development efficiency improved by the digital economy?
summary: The digital economy represents a core component of emerging productive forces. Using panel data for China spanning 2008–2022, this study measures the development of the digital economy and urban green development efficiency and empirically
content: The digital economy represents a core component of emerging productive forces. Using panel data for China spanning 2008–2022, this study measures the development of the digital economy and urban green development efficiency and empirically evaluates how digitalization influences green development outcomes. Results reveal that the digital economy significantly enhances urban green development efficiency, and this relationship remains robust across multiple specifications and endogeneity tests; the benefits of digitalization materialize gradually, producing a clear lagged effect; the impact varies across regions, with the strongest effect in Anhui and the weakest in Jiangsu, reflecting diminishing marginal returns; digitalization generates spatial spillovers that improve green development efficiency not only locally but also in adjacent areas; and mediation analysis indicates that the digital economy promotes green development efficiency partly by strengthening urban environmental regulation, which constrains environmentally intensive activities and incentivizes technological innovation.

title: Relational work in collaborative energy renovation: Understanding the role of tradespeople as middle actors
summary: Energy renovation policies have expanded rapidly, yet renovation rates remain below climate targets and policy outcomes remain uneven. One reason is that dominant policy approaches rely largely on techno-economic framings, paying insufficie
content: Energy renovation policies have expanded rapidly, yet renovation rates remain below climate targets and policy outcomes remain uneven. One reason is that dominant policy approaches rely largely on techno-economic framings, paying insufficient attention to the relational conditions through which renovation projects are organised and implemented. To address this gap, this article adopts a relational perspective and examines how collaborative energy renovation is organised through the case of Assisted Self-Renovation (Auto-Rénovation Accompagnée, ARA), an emerging collaborative approach in France based on close cooperation between households and tradespeople. Drawing on a mixed-methods study combining a survey of 220 building professionals and 30 semi-structured interviews, the findings identify four complementary dimensions of relational work through which tradespeople, as middle actors, organise collaboration with households: relational diagnosis, pedagogical work, relational and task selectivity, and continuous supervision. These practices are associated with stronger household engagement, positive perceptions of technical quality and safety, and greater access to ambitious energy renovation measures, particularly insulation interventions, with important implications for households facing energy vulnerability. Beyond ARA itself, the article argues that collaborative renovation provides a diagnostic lens through which broader transformations shaping energy renovation become visible. While respondents consistently identify positive technical and social outcomes, the wider development of these practices remains constrained by institutional misalignments in insurance, liability and the recognition of relational work. The article concludes that scaling up ambitious and socially inclusive energy renovation requires not only technological innovation and financial incentives but also greater recognition and support for the relational work undertaken by tradespeople.

title: A perspective on component-level digital twins for surface marine propulsion system health monitoring: need and feasibility
summary: Failures in marine propulsion systems pose significant safety and economic risks through loss-of-propulsion events. Although statistically infrequent, emerging maritime trends such as energy transition, alternative propulsion technologies,
content: Failures in marine propulsion systems pose significant safety and economic risks through loss-of-propulsion events. Although statistically infrequent, emerging maritime trends such as energy transition, alternative propulsion technologies, and Arctic navigation are expected to increase vulnerability to component failures, underscoring the need for advanced condition monitoring. This perspective article establishes component-level digital twins as an important but underexplored research direction. It introduces a scale-based characterisation of DTs from nano-level phenomena to process-level systems. It identifies the key barriers to practical implementation, including computational cost, dynamic modelling limitations, data scarcity and ownership constraints, communication challenges, and limited industry–academia collaboration. To address these gaps, the paper proposes the Digital Twin Research Hub (DTRH), a conceptual framework integrating risk-based prioritisation, physics-based modelling, surrogate modelling, and data-driven approaches. An experimentally validated bond graph-based simulation for torsional responses with placeholders for surrogate models is presented as an initiative. Finally, through a scholarly discussion, the study establishes the need for and feasibility of component-level DTs as an underexplored research direction for improving the reliability of marine propulsion systems through enhanced condition monitoring.

title: Financial Disclosure and Stock Market Reaction: Thematic Study of Investors’ Concern in Transparency of Corporate Firm
source: IIARD INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF BANKING AND FINANCE RESEARCH
summary: The thematic paper explored the relationship between financial disclosure practices and stock market reactions, with a particular focus on investor concerns regarding corporate transparency. The research examined how both financial and non-
content: The thematic paper explored the relationship between financial disclosure practices and stock market reactions, with a particular focus on investor concerns regarding corporate transparency. The research examined how both financial and non-financial disclosures influenced stock market behavior, investor perceptions, and market efficiency. Drawing on signaling theory, the study emphasized that transparency played a significant role in reducing information asymmetry and building trust between corporate firms and investors. The findings indicated that firms with comprehensive, accurate, and timely disclosures experienced positive stock market reactions, including greater price stability and increased investor confidence. In contrast, selective or delayed disclosures led to negative market reactions, often reflecting heightened uncertainty. Additionally, the paper highlighted the growing importance of non-financial disclosures, particularly environmental, social, and governance (ESG) factors, which shaped investor decisions and stock performance. The study concluded that corporate transparency was not only essential for regulatory compliance but also served as a strategic tool for improving investor relations, enhancing market efficiency, and ensuring long-term business success.

title: Quality Assessment of Sachet and Bottled Water Produced by a University and Selected Private Business Owners in Benin City, Nigeria
source: Journal of Science Research and Reviews
summary: Poor quality drinking water pose a public health risk to consumers and contribute to waterborne disease burden especially in developing countries. This study assessed the quality of sachet and bottled water produced by a university coded Un
content: Poor quality drinking water pose a public health risk to consumers and contribute to waterborne disease burden especially in developing countries. This study assessed the quality of sachet and bottled water produced by a university coded Uni and three private business owners (Lom, Olv and Tai) in Benin City, Nigeria. Microbiological analysis involved the use of traditional methods, while physicochemical properties, essential and toxic metals content of the samples (n = 24) were determined using standard methods. Kirby-Bauer disc diffusion method was used to test antibiotic susceptibility of the bacterial isolates. The total heterotrophic bacterial count and total fungal counts of the Uni brand of drinking water ranged between 2.48 - 2.64 and 2.00 - 3.70 log10CFU/mL, while other brands was 2.78 - 7.36 and 1.00 - 3.60 log10CFU/mL, respectively. No coliforms were detected in the Olv and Uni brands of drinking water. The physicochemical properties, essential and toxic metals content of the samples were below permissible limits stipulated by the World Health Organization (WHO) for drinking water, with some exceptions. Among the isolates, Staphylococcus aureus had the least multiple antibiotic resistant index of 0.0, whereas the highest involved Proteus mirabilis and Escherichia coli reported as 0.4 each. Although, the overall results indicate that the Uni branded product was relatively better than others, regulatory bodies such as National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC) should intensify its efforts in monitoring the production, storage, and distribution of sachet and bottled water to ensure strict compliance with international standards.

title: Assessing activated charcoal toxicity to key soil organisms: Microorganisms, Collembola and earthworms
summary: Although activated charcoal (AC) is a commonly used adjuvant in agrotechnical products, it is currently not comprehensively regulated. Under REACH, most terrestrial ecotoxicological tests are waived, as ACs are deemed chemically inert due t
content: Although activated charcoal (AC) is a commonly used adjuvant in agrotechnical products, it is currently not comprehensively regulated. Under REACH, most terrestrial ecotoxicological tests are waived, as ACs are deemed chemically inert due to their insolubility. Secondary physical effects are not considered. The aim of this study was therefore to evaluate holistically the ecotoxicological hazard of two ACs (hard coal- and wood-based). The effects on different microbial driven soil functions (OECD TG 216 – Nitrogen transformation, ISO 15685 – Potential nitrification, amoA abundance, ISO 20130 – Exoenzymatic activities), Collembola survival and reproduction (OECD TG 232) as well as earthworm avoidance (ISO 17512-1), survival, weight and reproduction (OECD TG 222) were observed in a concentration range from 10 to 1000 mg kg −1 . In a first stage of testing, a sandy soil was used. The organism group with the strongest ecotoxicological response was then exposed to the ACs in a silty soil to investigate the soil impact on the ecotoxicological effect. Overall, Collembola and earthworm reproduction were mostly unaffected, while earthworm avoidance behaviour was significantly triggered (LOEC 100 to 1000 mg kg −1 ). As the microbial driven soil functions were strongest affected, they were investigated further. Spore germination (ISO 10832) of arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi was added to the workflow for additional information but indicated no impairment. Nitrogen related processes were mostly not significantly affected. Exoenzymatic activities showed comparable ecotoxicological responses to ACs in silty and sandy soils (LOEC ≤10 mg kg −1 ), suggesting relevant secondary physical effects. At the highest concentration tested, these were discussed to partially interfere with the photometric measurements.

title: Economic benefit forecasting and parametric sensitivity analysis for shallow shale gas wells in the Zhaotong area using machine learning
summary: In shale gas development, Net Present Value (NPV) and Internal Rate of Return (IRR) are influenced by the coupling of multi-source geological and engineering parameters, and quantitative research on the marginal effects and risk thresholds
content: In shale gas development, Net Present Value (NPV) and Internal Rate of Return (IRR) are influenced by the coupling of multi-source geological and engineering parameters, and quantitative research on the marginal effects and risk thresholds of key parameters remains lacking. A deep feedforward neural network prediction model was constructed to achieve mapping from 19-dimensional features to NPV and IRR. The trained model was then utilized as a digital surrogate model to conduct univariate sensitivity analysis, quantifying the marginal impacts of parameters such as clay content, carbonate content, effective porosity, Poisson’s ratio, horizontal stress difference, and first-year average daily production on economic benefits. Cross-validated results indicate that the model achieves a mean R 2 of 0.6071 (±0.0957) for NPV prediction and 0.4168 (±0.1294) for IRR prediction. Furthermore, it identifies economic risk thresholds including 30% for clay content, 0.2 for Poisson’s ratio, and 17 MPa for horizontal stress difference, which are highly consistent with oilfield engineering experience. SHAP-based interaction analysis reveals that these thresholds are context-dependent, with interaction effects accounting for approximately 30%–32% of the main effects for clay content and horizontal stress difference.

title: Upcycling dental gypsum waste into enhanced plaster of Paris via chemical modification: Mechanical and microstructural study
summary: The primary composition of gypsum products is calcium sulfate dihydrate (CaSO 4 ·2 H 2 O), which is widely used in dentistry to create models, casts, and dies, forming the foundation of dental appliances and prostheses. Meanwhile, the dispo
content: The primary composition of gypsum products is calcium sulfate dihydrate (CaSO 4 ·2 H 2 O), which is widely used in dentistry to create models, casts, and dies, forming the foundation of dental appliances and prostheses. Meanwhile, the disposal of gypsum materials in dental facilities could lead to environmental pollution without sustainable management. Recycling gypsum materials might provide an opportunity. However, the properties could be compromised by the presence of contaminants during the process. This research explores the sustainable production of Plaster of Paris (POP) using gypsum from waste sources with the aim of enhancing their physical and mechanical properties using CaO, CaCl 2 , MgO, and MgCl 2 at varying amounts to improve the quality of POP produced from waste gypsum. Waste gypsum was thermally converted to produce CaSO 4 ·½H 2 O, followed by additive inclusion to analyze the setting time, compressive strength, diametral tensile strength, and Young’s modulus. Morphological analysis using scanning electron microscopy (SEM) revealed notable improvements in microstructure, with CaO showing the greatest effectiveness in reducing porosity and enhancing strength. Statistical analyses carried out by the ANOVA method indicated that gypsum modified with CaO performed much better with respect to mechanical and morphological properties. These findings demonstrate that oxide-enhanced renewable gypsum could be employed in sustainable dentistry while delivering high-performance upcycled materials.

title: Research on Environmental Stressors Effects and Stress‐Mitigation Technologies for Fish Transportation: A Review
summary: ABSTRACT Increasing consumer demand for fresh and nutritious food has contributed to the expansion of fresh food from aquaculture and live fish market particularly in Asian countries. However, fish undergo stress during live transportation
content: ABSTRACT Increasing consumer demand for fresh and nutritious food has contributed to the expansion of fresh food from aquaculture and live fish market particularly in Asian countries. However, fish undergo stress during live transportation due to the deterioration of water quality, temperature fluctuations, and excessive densities, and so forth. As the live fish transportation directly affects fish welfare and economic efficiency, developing efficient and appropriate transport strategies has become a critical focus in aquaculture research. This paper synthesizes the major stressors associated with live fish transport, including temperature, water quality, and density. It further explores the physiological and biochemical responses induced by transport stress, such as oxidative stress, immune suppression, and tissue damage. Additionally, current mitigation strategies are reviewed from multiple perspectives, such as selective genetic breeding, dietary supplementation, water quality optimization, waterless transport, and anesthetic‐assisted handling. Overall, this review provides a comprehensive reference for understanding and managing stress during live fish transport and offers a theoretical foundation for improving fish welfare and promoting the sustainable development of aquaculture logistics.

title: Metal‐Catalyzed Transformations of Carbon Dioxide Toward the Production of Commodity Chemicals
summary: This perspective examines advances in catalytic methods for converting CO 2 into value‐added commodity chemicals through a future‐facing research and development‐focused viewpoint. As such, select examples that we identify as representative
content: This perspective examines advances in catalytic methods for converting CO 2 into value‐added commodity chemicals through a future‐facing research and development‐focused viewpoint. As such, select examples that we identify as representative of the field in both mature and underdeveloped technologies are discussed. Transition‐metal catalysis has enabled progress toward the production of acrylic acid derivatives, methylmalonic acids, and cyclic carbonates, despite CO 2 ’s inherent stability. In contrast, other promising transformations, such as the synthesis of amino acids from CO 2 , remain limited by high costs, narrow substrate scope, and poor stereocontrol. Overall, CO 2 utilization offered significant potential as an economic means for sustainable chemical manufacturing while highlighting the need for further catalytic innovation.

title: Fiscal Transparency for Sustainable Development: The Global Evidence
summary: ABSTRACT Sustainable development (SD) has been a primary policy effort in government globally to address various key challenges in development and the environment. Transparency, as an accountability tool, is critical for stakeholders holdin
content: ABSTRACT Sustainable development (SD) has been a primary policy effort in government globally to address various key challenges in development and the environment. Transparency, as an accountability tool, is critical for stakeholders holding government administrations accountable for SD policy outcomes. Given the very limited literature on the role of administrative transparency in SD, this study creates a comprehensive global panel database covering the period from 2006 to 2022 to examine the effect of fiscal transparency on sustainability policy performance. The results indicate a significant role of developing transparency institutions in promoting SD goals, and distinctive effect of such development in countries of different development stages. The findings point to different paths for achieving accountability goals under different institutional conditions, which is significant for establishing and strengthening accountability enhancement strategies for policy outcomes.

title: Does regional integration strategy promote green innovation? Evidence from China's Yangtze River Delta integration
summary: The implementation of regional integration strategy has facilitated the rapid development of the regional economy and society; however, its potential to promote green innovation within the region still requires further investigation. Focusi
content: The implementation of regional integration strategy has facilitated the rapid development of the regional economy and society; however, its potential to promote green innovation within the region still requires further investigation. Focusing on China's macro-regional strategy of the Yangtze River Delta (YRD) integration, this study treats its rollout as a quasi-natural experiment. We empirically investigate its effect on green innovation by applying a multi-period difference-in-differences model to urban panel data (2004–2020) from six provinces and one city in East China. And the intermediary influence mechanism was analyzed by TOE theoretical framework. The results show that the YRD integration strategy can significantly promote urban green innovation, and the effect is more significant for the cities with a population of <5 million. The YRD integration strategy can promote urban green innovation by improving the information level, increasing government support and strict environmental regulations.

title: Balancing Sustainability and Digitalization: How Country FinTech Rank Moderates the ESG –Firm Value Relationship Amid Controversies
source: Corporate Social Responsibility and Environmental Management
summary: ABSTRACT This paper investigates the impact of ESG performance and ESG washing on firm value within the context of rapidly evolving digital financial systems. Although ESG disclosure has become central to corporate decision‐making, concerns
content: ABSTRACT This paper investigates the impact of ESG performance and ESG washing on firm value within the context of rapidly evolving digital financial systems. Although ESG disclosure has become central to corporate decision‐making, concerns regarding ESG washing have raised doubts about the credibility of reported sustainability practices and their true valuation effects. At the same time, the rise of FinTech development may reshape how markets process and price ESG‐related information, yet this interaction remains underexplored in the literature. Using panel data from global ESG Leaders Index firms between 2018 and 2023, fixed‐effects regression models and industry‐sensitivity robustness checks capture the interplay between ESG, ESG controversies, FinTech development, and firm value. Results show that higher ESG performance and reduced exposure to controversies significantly enhance firm value. Furthermore, country‐level FinTech development strengthens the positive valuation effect of credible ESG performance, indicating that digitally advanced financial ecosystems enhance investors' ability to distinguish between firms with substantive sustainability practices and those engaging in ESG washing. Industry‐sensitive sectors also exhibit stronger ESG–value linkages. For managers, the findings highlight the importance of verifiable ESG practices, particularly in sensitive industries. For policymakers and investors, the study underscores the relevance of FinTech maturity and industry context when assessing ESG disclosure credibility. This study contributes to the literature by examining the ESG washing–value relationship within the broader framework of country‐level FinTech development.

title: Fall-related injuries in long-term oxygen therapy: Incidence and predictive factors
source: Annals of the American Thoracic Society
summary: INTRODUCTION: Fall-related injuries are a common cause of morbidity and impaired quality of life among patients with severe respiratory disease. Use of long-term oxygen therapy (LTOT) may be associated with a further increased risk. METHODS
content: INTRODUCTION: Fall-related injuries are a common cause of morbidity and impaired quality of life among patients with severe respiratory disease. Use of long-term oxygen therapy (LTOT) may be associated with a further increased risk. METHODS: This was a longitudinal study of patients starting LTOT between 2006 and 2023 in the Swedish DISCOVERY cohort. Rates of healthcare contact due to three types of fall-related injuries (distal radius fracture, hip fracture, and skull trauma) were compared to those of age- and sex-matched population controls using nationwide registries. For patients on LTOT, pre-identified potentially predictive factors were analyzed against a composite outcome of any fall-related injury using Cox and Fine-Gray regression, independently, adjusting for age, sex and Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI), and in a joint model adjusting for all predictive factors. RESULTS: A total 16,915 patients with LTOT (mean age 76±9 years, 57% female, 63% underlying COPD) and an equal number of matched controls were included. Compared with controls, LTOT patients had increased overall rates of both hospitalizations (15.5 vs 7.3 per 100 patient-years) and outpatient (16.9 vs 13.6 per 100 patient-years) healthcare contacts due to fall-related injuries, driven by hip fractures and skull trauma, whereas distal radius fractures were more common among patients without LTOT. The strongest independent predictive factors for fall-related injury during LTOT were history of previous fall-related injury (HR1.8; 95% confidence interval 1.7-2.0) and increased CCI. The overall predictive capability of the model was poor (C-statistic 0.65). CONCLUSION: Patients on LTOT have a high rate of health care contacts due to hip fractures and skull trauma, but whether this increase is caused by use of oxygen equipment or underlying frailty remains unknown. While individual falls were difficult to predict, indicators such as previous fall injury and comorbidities, may inform optimized follow-up and interventions aimed at mitigating risk.
