title: Human development under fiscal, financial, and environmental constraints: Evidence from SAARC economies
summary: Type of the article: Research ArticleAbstractThe present study investigates the macroeconomic determinants of human development in eight South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC) economies during the period 1990–2023, with sp
content: Type of the article: Research ArticleAbstractThe present study investigates the macroeconomic determinants of human development in eight South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC) economies during the period 1990–2023, with special emphasis on the roles of public debt, economic growth, financial development, and environmental degradation. A fixed-effects estimation with Driscoll–Kraay robust standard errors and Dumitrescu–Hurlin panel causality tests on an unbalanced panel dataset of 204 observations is used to test the long-run relationships and dynamic interactions among the variables. The results indicate that economic growth and financial development are important and robust determinants of human development. The findings underscore the importance of raising income and deepening finance for the improvement of human capabilities. The effects of public debt on development depend on fiscal governance and the productive use of borrowed resources. Public debt does not have a significant independent effect once well-known econometric problems are accounted for. Environmental degradation is a serious threat to human development and a complex illustration of the link between industrial transformation and sustainability in developing economies. The study highlights the importance of integrated policies in the SAARC economies for promoting inclusive growth, financial inclusion, fiscal prudence, and environmental sustainability.

title: Urban oasis living lab: a hybrid approach to climate-resilient urban agriculture in Beirut
summary: Introduction As cities face increasing resource constraints, environmental pressures, and food-system vulnerabilities, urban agriculture is gaining recognition as a practical approach to enhancing climate resilience and sustainability. Howe
content: Introduction As cities face increasing resource constraints, environmental pressures, and food-system vulnerabilities, urban agriculture is gaining recognition as a practical approach to enhancing climate resilience and sustainability. However, many urban agriculture initiatives remain fragmented, often focusing on isolated ecological or technical interventions without fully integrating resource management, stakeholder engagement, and long-term resilience mechanisms. Methods To address these gaps, the Urban Oasis was established by the Environment and Sustainable Development Unit (ESDU) at the American University of Beirut (AUB), with support from the Khalifa International Award for Date Palm and Agricultural Innovation. An abandoned animal house was transformed into a multifunctional living lab for research, innovation, education, and community engagement through a structured five-phase process comprising participatory design, site rehabilitation, technology activation, engagement and applied learning, and continuous monitoring and evaluation. The resulting living lab combines sustainable agriculture practices, circular economy principles, low-impact infrastructure, smart sensing systems, artificial intelligence, and automated controls. Results Over 3 years of operation, the Urban Oasis produced approximately 8,500 kg of food, recovers approximately 480,000 liters of water annually, and avoids an estimated 1.26 tons of carbon dioxide emissions each year. More than 5,000 individuals have engaged with the testbed, and 62.7% of participants reported adopting or willingness to adopt at least one demonstrated practice in their daily lives. The initiative has also supported academic research, student projects, and scientific publications. Discussion The Urban Oasis demonstrates how urban agriculture can evolve beyond food production into an integrated resilience framework connecting resource efficiency, community engagement, education, and technological innovation. As a scalable and adaptable model, it offers insights for advancing sustainable and climate-resilient urban development across the Middle East and North Africa region and beyond.

title: The world is being fed at the expense of nature: A remote sensing based global assessment from 2000 to 2019
summary: Understanding agricultural productivity dynamics is essential for evaluating the global capacity to achieve food security while safeguarding nature. This requires tracking food production relative to natural resource use. The Comprehensive
content: Understanding agricultural productivity dynamics is essential for evaluating the global capacity to achieve food security while safeguarding nature. This requires tracking food production relative to natural resource use. The Comprehensive Assessment of Water Management in Agriculture (CAWMA), a landmark CGIAR-led study by over 700 scientists, presents six scenarios for the future of food production; its optimal scenario outlines a pathway to meeting food, economic, and environmental objectives by 2050. Using satellite remote sensing from validated global datasets, we derived spatially explicit trends in key agricultural variables from 2000 to 2019 and compared these against CAWMA optimal scenario projections. Our findings show that the world has substantially deviated from this scenario, aligning with more pessimistic outlooks. Global agricultural production increased by 24.3%, nearly meeting the projected 26.2% growth in food demand, but through an 11.5% expansion of cropland area, three times faster than the projected 3.6%, and at least 15.0% increase in irrigated area, more than two times the projected 6.1%. Crop water consumption rose by 25.3% against a projection of 7.4%. Land productivity improved by only 11.6% versus a projected 21.7%, and water productivity declined by 1.6% against a projected increase of 12.9%. These trends confirm continued resource-intensive habits, risking nature and undermining long-term water and food security. To redirect these trajectories, we recommend grounding agricultural scenarios in empirical evidence integrating remote sensing with statistical data; regularly updating productivity models; improving data accessibility for policymakers; shifting toward systemic transformation of food production; and adopting locally differentiated yet globally coordinated responses.

title: Push–pull–block framework for lycopene biosynthesis: a comprehensive review of metabolic engineering strategies in Saccharomyces cerevisiae
summary: Lycopene is a high-value carotenoid widely utilized in food, pharmaceutical, nutraceutical, and cosmetic industries because of its strong antioxidant properties and associated health benefits. Among microbial hosts, Saccharomyces cerevisiae
content: Lycopene is a high-value carotenoid widely utilized in food, pharmaceutical, nutraceutical, and cosmetic industries because of its strong antioxidant properties and associated health benefits. Among microbial hosts, Saccharomyces cerevisiae has emerged as a promising platform for sustainable lycopene biosynthesis due to its Generally Recognized as Safe status, well-characterized metabolism, and compatibility with industrial-scale fermentation processes. However, efficient lycopene production in yeast remains constrained by limited precursor availability, metabolic flux imbalance, competing pathways, redox stress, and intracellular toxicity associated with carotenoid accumulation. This review comprehensively summarizes current metabolic engineering strategies for enhancing lycopene biosynthesis in S. cerevisiae through an integrated “push–pull–block” framework. Push strategies focus on increasing precursor supply, acetyl-CoA availability, mevalonate pathway flux, and NADPH regeneration. Pull strategies emphasize pathway optimization through promoter engineering, gene dosage tuning, enzyme scaffolding, and heterologous carotenoid pathway enhancement to improve carbon flux toward lycopene biosynthesis. Block strategies target the suppression of competing sterol pathways, relief of feedback inhibition, and redirection of metabolic resources toward carotenoid accumulation. In addition, emerging approaches involving stress mitigation, lipid droplet engineering, adaptive laboratory evolution, dynamic regulation, controlled fermentation, and multi-omics-guided systems metabolic engineering are discussed as next-generation solutions for improving industrial lycopene production. Collectively, this review provides a systems-level perspective on current advances and future opportunities in engineering S. cerevisiae as an efficient microbial cell factory for sustainable lycopene biosynthesis.

title: Environmental Transparency Through Digital Transformation: Evidence on Carbon Disclosure Quality From China's Heavy‐Polluting Firms
source: Corporate Social Responsibility and Environmental Management
summary: ABSTRACT The rise of digital transformation (DT) has become an important driver of transparency in corporate environmental disclosure. Whether and how DT is related to the improvement of carbon information disclosure quality, particularly i
content: ABSTRACT The rise of digital transformation (DT) has become an important driver of transparency in corporate environmental disclosure. Whether and how DT is related to the improvement of carbon information disclosure quality, particularly in heavily polluting firms that may have both information and symbolic roles, is still controversial. Based on the resource‐based view, information asymmetry theory, and signaling theory, this study examines the association between DT and carbon information disclosure quality in Chinese A‐share listed heavy‐polluting firms from 2017 to 2024. Using a multidimensional CIDQ index and panel data models, this study finds that DT is positively associated with carbon information disclosure quality. Additional analyses suggest that this relationship is linked to external monitoring channels, including media attention and audit effort, is stronger under higher product market competition, and is further strengthened when external monitoring and competition jointly increase. The results at the component level also reveal that the association is more obvious in carbon‐related business practices, carbon governance, and carbon performance rather than the disclosure carrier, which illustrates that DT may be more strongly associated with the content of carbon disclosure than with its reporting format or disclosure channel. Further analyses suggest a positive association between DT‐enabled disclosure quality and firms' environmental performance. Other analyses highlight that such an effect is more evident in state‐owned enterprises and areas with more advanced digital infrastructure. The study contributes to research on DT and environmental disclosure by showing both the transparency‐enhancing potential and the limitations of digitalized carbon reporting.

title: Orchard and storage-dependent metabolic and transcriptional regulation of superficial scald in ‘Packham’s Triumph’ pears
summary: Superficial scald (SS), a chilling-induced peel disorder, limits the storability and marketability of cold-stored ‘Packham’s Triumph’ pears. This study combined gene expression and non-polar metabolomic profiling to elucidate orchard- and s
content: Superficial scald (SS), a chilling-induced peel disorder, limits the storability and marketability of cold-stored ‘Packham’s Triumph’ pears. This study combined gene expression and non-polar metabolomic profiling to elucidate orchard- and storage-specific mechanisms regulating SS development. Pears were sourced from three commercial orchards and stored under regular atmosphere (RA), controlled atmosphere (CA), or stepwise cooling (SWC). Controlled atmosphere (CA) consistently provided the greatest suppression of SS, whereas the effectiveness of stepwise cooling (SWC) varied among orchards. Gene expression analysis showed that storage atmosphere regulated stress- and senescence-related genes, with antioxidant-associated genes (GST and GPx) generally enhanced under CA and SWC, while lipid degradation- and senescence-associated genes (LPS, LOX, and SGR) exhibited storage- and orchard-dependent responses. Metabolomic analyses revealed coordinated changes in farnesyl conjugates, hydroxycinnamoyl acyl esters, diacylglycerols, triacylglycerols, phytosterol conjugates, and sphingolipids under scald-suppressive storage conditions. Correlation network analysis further identified coordinated associations between stress-responsive genes, particularly 9-cis-epoxycarotenoid dioxygenase (NCED), and metabolites involved in membrane lipid remodeling and secondary metabolism. These findings improve our understanding of the molecular basis of superficial scald in pear and identify candidate gene and metabolite biomarkers that could support orchard-specific scald risk assessment and the development of targeted postharvest storage strategies.

title: Towards transformative policy mixes for healthy, sustainable diets in a multi-level governance context
summary: Abstract Transitioning towards healthier, more sustainable food environments is critical to mitigate diet-related chronic diseases and environmental harm. Coordinated governmental action supporting this transition is often hindered by fragm
content: Abstract Transitioning towards healthier, more sustainable food environments is critical to mitigate diet-related chronic diseases and environmental harm. Coordinated governmental action supporting this transition is often hindered by fragmented competences across policy fields and governance levels. Different strands of literature address this issue from within their respective disciplines, with some excelling in their empirical approach, others being more firmly grounded in theory, and still others emphasizing the legal-institutional dimension. This study aimed to strengthen the identification and assessment of policy mixes governing food environments by layering these disciplinary approaches. More precisely, it combined the Food Environment Policy Index (Food-EPI) from public health literature with the Six Policy Intervention Points framework (6PIP) from sustainability transitions literature, supported by constitutional law analysis. Illustrated by the case of federal Belgium, the study mapped 200 policy instruments and 31 strategies across 8 jurisdictions, followed by an assessment of policy intensity by a panel of 51 experts. Instrument types and intervention points were subsequently characterized, with balance across these serving as a measure of policy mix comprehensiveness. The results showed hotspots of policy activity in public procurement and norm management, while gaps existed in zoning laws and advertising regulations. These patterns parallel a strong focus on niche stimulation and acceleration, contrasted with limited regime-destabilizing measures. The 6PIP lens further highlights the absence of measures addressing socio-economic repercussions of destabilization — a precursor of destabilization measures and an important blind spot not captured by the Food-EPI lens alone. Together, these findings reflect a broader governance paradigm observed across other EU member states. The integrated layered approach elaborated here is meaningful for future applications, particularly when embedded in a stronger contextualization of these prevailing governance modes, actor constellations and corresponding transition dynamics.

title: The Trout Paradox: Scenarios for Managing Introduced Salmonids in New Zealand
source: New Zealand Journal of Marine and Freshwater Research
summary: Introduced salmonids such as trout and salmon occupy a paradoxical position in New Zealand; celebrated as iconic sport fish yet condemned as invasive species that threaten native freshwater biodiversity. Motivated by an economic impact stud
content: Introduced salmonids such as trout and salmon occupy a paradoxical position in New Zealand; celebrated as iconic sport fish yet condemned as invasive species that threaten native freshwater biodiversity. Motivated by an economic impact study of recreational fishing on Te Manahuna Mackenzie Basin hydro canals—the country's most popular salmonid fishery—we explore scenarios for the future management of trout in New Zealand. While conservationists have long highlighted the ecological harms of salmonids, their recreation and tourism significance complicates calls for eradication. In this ‘thought experiment’, we use scenario planning as a heuristic device to interrogate these contradictions, outlining two deliberately provocative scenarios: (1) Nationwide eradication of trout, enabled by emerging biocontrol technologies and intensive management; (2) A compromise strategy of ‘trout utilisation zones’, where populations are deliberately contained in artificial or highly modified freshwater systems to sustain angling, tourism, wellbeing and food security benefits while enabling biodiversity recovery elsewhere. By juxtaposing these features with the status quo, we highlight trade‐offs among ecological, socio‐cultural and economic values. Considering improbable scenarios illuminates governance tensions over the place of salmonids in New Zealand's freshwaters, and importantly, identifies technical, organisational and governance competencies required to operationalise alternative futures for their management.

title: Financial Technologies and Market Volatility: Dynamic Connectedness between FinTech and Traditional Markets
source: Journal of Central Banking Theory and Practice
summary: Abstract This study examines the dynamic volatility spillover between financial technologies and traditional and alternative financial markets. The analysis utilizes daily data covering the period from January 2018 to March 2026 for FinTech
content: Abstract This study examines the dynamic volatility spillover between financial technologies and traditional and alternative financial markets. The analysis utilizes daily data covering the period from January 2018 to March 2026 for FinTech ETFs, the Nasdaq, Bitcoin, and gold markets. Interconnectivity among financial markets was analyzed using the time-varying parameter VAR (TVP-VAR) connectedness approach. The findings indicate the presence of a moderate and time-varying connectivity structure among the markets. In particular, a strong interaction was observed between the FinTech and Nasdaq markets, while Bitcoin was found to play a significant role as a volatility transmitter during certain periods. The gold market, on the other hand, generally exhibited more stable and limited interactions. Additionally, the study found that financial market linkages increase during periods of crisis and uncertainty. These results highlight that the transmission of volatility across financial markets has a dynamic structure and that portfolio diversification strategies should be evaluated accordingly. By examining FinTech markets alongside other major asset classes, the study provides a timely and comprehensive contribution to the literature.

title: ICBBM 2025 in Rio de Janeiro: A synthesis of recent advances, current gaps and emerging directions in bio-based building materials
summary: The 6th International Conference on Bio-Based Building Materials (ICBBM 2025), held in Rio de Janeiro in June 2025, was the first edition organised outside Europe and reflected the growing internationalisation of the field. The proceedings,
content: The 6th International Conference on Bio-Based Building Materials (ICBBM 2025), held in Rio de Janeiro in June 2025, was the first edition organised outside Europe and reflected the growing internationalisation of the field. The proceedings, published in RILEM Bookseries Volumes 60 and 61, gather 144 peer-reviewed papers across eleven thematic sessions covering manufacturing, natural fibres, innovative binders, durability, modelling, environmental assessment, structural applications, earth construction and hygrothermal behaviour. This Technical Letter provides an editorial synthesis of the conference and critically analyses the maturity of the different research areas, the contradictions between studies and the gap between demonstrated evidence and stated claims. Nine structural gaps are identified, including long-term durability, harmonisation of life-cycle assessment and biogenic-carbon accounting, standards and codes, biological variability and building-scale demonstration. The paper also discusses future research trajectories and repositions bio-based construction as an engineered carbon-storage technology with implications for durability, certification and climate mitigation.

title: Metal additive manufacturing for unmanned aerial vehicle propulsion: a narrative review of recent advances in gas turbine systems
summary: Metal additive manufacturing (MAM) is revolutionizing the design and production of high-performance components across the aerospace sector. This narrative review examines recent research on gas turbine propulsion systems for unmanned aerial
content: Metal additive manufacturing (MAM) is revolutionizing the design and production of high-performance components across the aerospace sector. This narrative review examines recent research on gas turbine propulsion systems for unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), with a particular focus on the transformative role of metal additive manufacturing (MAM) in enabling lighter, more efficient, and more complex engine architectures. The study analyzes the operating principles, performance characteristics, and applications of turbojet, turbofan, and turboprop engines while highlighting key technological advances in hybridization, cycle optimization, and advanced manufacturing. Particular attention is given to MAM of high-temperature alloys (e.g., Inconel, titanium aluminides) and the integration of topology-optimized lattice structures, internal cooling channels, and monolithic rotors. Recent studies on additive manufacturing (AM) for drone components—including metal-doped plastics, composite filaments, and high-performance polymers—provide complementary insights into material selection, structural integrity, and functional integration that are directly relevant to gas turbine development. The study also incorporates the emerging roles of Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) in evaluating environmental sustainability and the use of machine learning for advanced fault diagnostics. Drawing on thermodynamic analyses, experimental studies, and modelling efforts, this review identifies current challenges and future directions in MAM for UAV propulsion, and briefly discusses potential cross-fertilization with biomedical AM, where similar challenges in process control, microstructure optimization, and post-processing are being addressed.

title: Through the Roof and Smack Into the Planet: Mobility and Deep (Un-)Sustainability, California, 1947–2020s
summary: California is often portrayed as a global leader in environmental policy, yet its transportation sector remains the state's largest source of greenhouse gas emissions and a persistent obstacle to meeting climate targets. This article argues
content: California is often portrayed as a global leader in environmental policy, yet its transportation sector remains the state's largest source of greenhouse gas emissions and a persistent obstacle to meeting climate targets. This article argues that this contradiction can only be understood through a long-term historical analysis of California's transportation system. Focusing on the period from the late 1940s to the 2020s, it traces how post-war infrastructure investment, automobility, suburbanisation, and growth-oriented policy frameworks produced enduring patterns of high mobility demand, material throughput, and environmental overshoot. Combining quantitative indicators with qualitative analysis of policies, institutions, and socio-technical imaginaries, the study uses the Safe and Just Space framework as an analytical lens to assess the sustainability of transport trajectories over time. It shows that successive waves of environmental regulation and technological innovation mitigated specific impacts without altering the structural drivers of car dependence. The article concludes that California's transport challenges are historically embedded and that achieving deep sustainability will require confronting these long-standing structural dynamics.

title: Structure–Performance Relationships in Newly Designed Linear Polyamines for Advanced CO2 Sorption
summary: Establishing structure–performance relationships is key to designing next‑generation CO2 sorbents with high efficiency and durability. This study investigates two newly designed linear polyamines, poly(hexyleneimine) (PHI) and poly(undecyle
content: Establishing structure–performance relationships is key to designing next‑generation CO2 sorbents with high efficiency and durability. This study investigates two newly designed linear polyamines, poly(hexyleneimine) (PHI) and poly(undecyleneimine) (PUI), obtained from polyamide feedstocks and developed as innovative polymer‑based materials for advanced CO2 capture. Their sorption capacity, desorption kinetics and thermal stability were evaluated in unsupported and fumed‑silica‑supported forms to elucidate how backbone architecture and amine spacing govern performance. Thermogravimetric analysis revealed that unsupported PHI and PUI effectively sorb and desorb CO2 at 110°C and 50°C, respectively. Cryo-milling selectively enhanced PUI performance, highlighting the critical influence of molecular architecture on amine site accessibility. Support impregnation significantly improved low-temperature performance: supported PHI achieved a maximum uptake of 1.67 mmol·g-1 at 70°C with an amine efficiency of 0.34, comparable to commercial linear poly(ethyleneimine) (L-PEI), while supported-PUI reached 0.85 mmol·g-1 at 50°C. Both polyamines demonstrated superior resistance to oxidative degradation compared to L-PEI, attributed to their higher density of amine spacers. Overall, PHI and PUI demonstrate how molecular design directly translates/impacts CO2 sorption performance, positioning these linear polyamines as robust, thermally reversible sorbents for advanced carbon‑capture applications.

title: Comparative Models of Green FinTech in Net Zero Transitions
summary: The international obligation to reach the net-zero level of emissions has enhanced the requirement to develop new financial tools that would be able to raise funds to support sustainable development. One of the factors in this transition ha
content: The international obligation to reach the net-zero level of emissions has enhanced the requirement to develop new financial tools that would be able to raise funds to support sustainable development. One of the factors in this transition has been financial technology (FinTech) that has employed digital innovation and financial services to help provide sustainable investment, transparency, and efficiency in capital allocation. Green FinTech is the intersection of FinTech innovations and environmentally sustainable goals, especially those of assisting climate mitigation and climate adaptation policies. The chapter analyzes the examples of green FinTech, and the way they facilitate net-zero transitions. Based on theoretical frameworks and new trends in the world, the chapter outlines the major models such as digital green lending systems, carbon markets facilitated by blockchain, AI-based climate risk analytics, and crowdfunding solutions to sustainable projects.

title: Biogenic AgNPs: Integrated Evaluation of Their Antibacterial Efficacy, Photocatalytic Degradation Capability, Optical Features, and Electrical Transport Mechanisms
summary: ABSTRACT A comprehensive evaluation of silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) synthesized through an eco‐friendly, plant‐mediated method is represented. It delivers a rare, single‐system multifunctional evaluation correlating structural, optical band
content: ABSTRACT A comprehensive evaluation of silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) synthesized through an eco‐friendly, plant‐mediated method is represented. It delivers a rare, single‐system multifunctional evaluation correlating structural, optical band‐gap, biological, photocatalytic, and detailed electrical transport mechanisms within a unified biogenic AgNP configuration. The AgNPs, prepared at three concentrations (NP1, NP2, NP3), were tested against Staphylococcus aureus and Escherichia coli . The nanoparticles showed clear antibacterial activity, with E. coli exhibiting higher susceptibility due to its thinner peptidoglycan layer. Photocatalytic experiments revealed that the nanoparticles efficiently degraded methyl orange (MO) and tetracycline (TC) under visible light, achieving degradation efficiencies of approximately 85% and 88%, respectively. Kinetic modelling confirmed pseudo–first‐order reaction behaviour. Optical characterization through UV‐Visible spectroscopy indicated well‐defined surface plasmon resonance (SPR) peaks and size‐dependent band gaps ranging from 2.99 to 3.10 eV. Additional analyses of Urbach energy (E U ), refractive index, and spectral broadening highlighted differences in structural order and nanoparticle stability. Electrical transport measurements demonstrated semiconducting characteristics governed by Mott variable range hopping in dc mode and correlated barrier hopping (CBH) in ac mode, with temperature and magnetic field significantly influencing conductivity. Collectively, the results show that green‐synthesized AgNPs possess a combination of strong antibacterial action, high photocatalytic efficiency, tunable optical features, and disorder‐dependent charge transport.

title: Proof-of-concept and economic feasibility evaluation of carbonic acid-based electrochemical system for simultaneous CO₂ utilization and hydrogen production
summary: The rising urgency to decarbonize industrial operations has led to the development of a novel electrochemical platform known as the Carbonic Acid-Based Electricity Generation (CAEG) system, designed to convert captured carbon dioxide into h
content: The rising urgency to decarbonize industrial operations has led to the development of a novel electrochemical platform known as the Carbonic Acid-Based Electricity Generation (CAEG) system, designed to convert captured carbon dioxide into hydrogen and value-added by-products under ambient conditions. Unlike conventional CO₂ electrolysis systems that require continuous external electrical energy input, the CAEG system operates through spontaneous galvanic reactions driven by carbonic acid, enabling simultaneous CO₂ utilization, electricity generation, hydrogen production, and mineral by-product recovery within a single platform. The system utilizes weak carbonic acid as the electrolyte and a sacrificial zinc anode to drive spontaneous electrochemical reactions without external power input. Three cell configurations were evaluated, and the optimal setup comprised an iridium oxide-coated titanium cathode, a potassium ion selective membrane (Flemion F8080K), and 1 M KOH anolyte. The optimized system achieved stable operation for 264 h with an average power density of 2.01 mW cm⁻², corresponding to a current density of 4.02 mA cm⁻², and a hydrogen Faradaic efficiency of 76.5%. Average product yields of 0.10 g day⁻¹ hydrogen, 9.06 g day⁻¹ KHCO₃, and 4.08 g day⁻¹ ZnO were obtained. Feed gas studies further revealed that the presence of trace nitric oxides significantly enhanced hydrogen production and electrical power generation, highlighting the influence of representative anthropogenic impurities on CAEG performance. A techno-economic analysis of a 10 kW modular CAEG system projected an annual revenue of USD 562,000 with a return on investment within six years, driven primarily by KHCO₃ and ZnO sales. The novelty of this work lies in the integration of CO₂ utilization, hydrogen production, electricity generation, and recovery of commercially valuable mineral products within a self-powered electrochemical system, combined with long-term operational validation, evaluation under simulated industrial gas compositions, and preliminary techno-economic assessment. These findings demonstrate the potential of the CAEG system as a self-powered platform for simultaneous electricity generation, hydrogen production, and CO₂ utilization, providing a promising pathway towards industrial decarbonization and circular carbon utilization.

title: An EPD-Based Comparative Study Life Cycle Assessment of Wood-Based Materials Used in Furniture Production
source: Gazi Üniversitesi Fen Bilimleri Dergisi Part C Tasarım ve Teknoloji
summary: This study comparatively evaluates the life cycle–based environmental performance of wood-based materials used in furniture production. Five material types were analysed: solid sawn timber, raw particleboard, coated particleboard, raw MDF,
content: This study comparatively evaluates the life cycle–based environmental performance of wood-based materials used in furniture production. Five material types were analysed: solid sawn timber, raw particleboard, coated particleboard, raw MDF, and lacquered MDF. The data were obtained from the open-access EPD (Environmental Product Declaration) archive of the One Click LCA platform, and the analysis focused on the cradle-to-gate (A1–A3) stages using Global Warming Potential (GWP) as the main indicator. The findings reveal that solid sawn timber has the lowest GWP value (24 kg CO₂/m³), while lacquered MDF exhibits nearly twenty times higher emissions. This disparity is primarily attributed to the energy intensity, resin content, and surface finishing processes in manufacturing. The results emphasize that sustainability assessment should not be limited to material type but must encompass the entire production chain, including processing parameters and energy sources. Furthermore, the limited accessibility of EPD data has been identified as a major constraint in comparative environmental analyses. It is therefore recommended that all manufacturers develop product-specific EPDs and make them publicly available to enhance transparency and promote sustainability-driven competition across the furniture industry.

title: Warning and green labels versus Nutri-Score: visual attention and product evaluation in a binational eye-tracking study
summary: Front-of-package labeling (FOPL) is intended to improve consumer awareness of nutritional quality and encourage healthier choices. In 2020, Germany and Israel implemented distinct FOPL systems: Israel introduced mandatory red warning labels
content: Front-of-package labeling (FOPL) is intended to improve consumer awareness of nutritional quality and encourage healthier choices. In 2020, Germany and Israel implemented distinct FOPL systems: Israel introduced mandatory red warning labels with a voluntary green positive label for healthy foods, while Germany adopted the Nutri-Score. This study compared visual attention to these two FOPL schemes and their impact on product perception in a binational context. We conducted a comparative eye-tracking study with 223 participants (112 in Germany, 111 in Israel). Each participant viewed food package images, each displaying either a Nutri-Score or a red warning or green label, while their eye-movements were recorded. Then, participants rated perceived product healthfulness, expected taste, and purchase intention and completed questionnaires on eating habits, nutritional knowledge, and label understanding and usage. Outcomes were analyzed with mixed-effects models and t -tests. Label system and familiarity influenced visual attention and consumer evaluations. Red warning labels draw more attention when novel, while familiar labels are noticed faster but scrutinized less. Perceived healthfulness of poorer nutritional products was higher under Nutri-Score compared to explicit warnings. Participants also rated warning labels as easier to understand and more helpful for making healthy choices than Nutri-Score labels in both countries. These findings underscore the importance of empirical evaluation of both attention-catching ability and user comprehension in designing effective FOPL interventions.

title: Governance through intelligence: how smart cities enhance new quality productive forces
summary: Although digitalization has progressed rapidly, there is still a limited empirical understanding of how smart governance contributes to the evolution of new quality productive forces (NQPF) in developing countries. This study exploits the i
content: Although digitalization has progressed rapidly, there is still a limited empirical understanding of how smart governance contributes to the evolution of new quality productive forces (NQPF) in developing countries. This study exploits the implementation of the smart city initiative as a policy shock and draws on panel data from Chinese cities spanning 2007 to 2019. The results indicate that smart city development is associated with a statistically significant increase in the growth of NQPF. Moreover, the estimated effects are stronger for new labor tools and new labor objects than for new labor force. Specifically, smart city initiatives facilitate greater governmental digital subsidy support for strategic emerging industries, significantly increasing both the breadth and depth of digital subsidies they receive. Additionally, smart city policies improve the local digital development environment while attracting digital enterprises and talent, fostering spatial agglomeration. Moreover, the influence of smart city development on strengthening NQPF varies according to a city’s degree of innovation capacity and the extent of focus it receives from both governmental agencies and the public. Notably, the policy-driven promotion of NQPF through smart city initiatives is more substantial in large urban centers, non-resource-based cities, and municipalities that do not belong to the category of old industrial bases.

title: EVALUATION OF STATISTICAL TRENDS OF THE COST OF DEBT CAPITAL IN INDIA FOR ENERGY AND INFRASTRUCTURE PROJECTS
summary: Debt financing is a core component of energy and infrastructure finance in most countries of the world and has direct impact on project valuation, feasibility, and profitability. This work analyses openly available data from the last one de
content: Debt financing is a core component of energy and infrastructure finance in most countries of the world and has direct impact on project valuation, feasibility, and profitability. This work analyses openly available data from the last one decade on the costs of debt finance in India, focusing on two major instrument classes - bank loans and debt securities like bonds issued over the last one decade. Bank loan rate data from the Reserve Bank of India from 2014 to 2025 show that loan interest rates have ranged from 8.75 ± 1.33% per annum to 11.18 ± 0.88% per annum, depending on type of bank considered, with private sector bank interests showing the highest range of values. The analysis of 10-, 15-, 30- and 40-year government bonds as a form of debt security shows that the annualized bond yields have been 7.25 ± 0.80%, 7.36 ± 0.60%, 7.43 ± 0.55% and 7.18 ± 0.28% respectively. Thus, in general, the bond yields have been lower than the bank lending rates. Comparison with 10-year bond yield data from 14 economies shows that developed economies have typically had bond yields much lower than that for India and other developing markets, indicating that infrastructure finance is costlier to access in developing nations where most infrastructure build out is needed to support their development objectives.

title: Business cycles, renewable energy, and short-term dynamics of carbon emissions: Evidence of asymmetric output gaps across advanced economies
summary: This study examines the short-term dynamics of CO₂ emissions in advanced economies in relation to business cycles, energy intensity, the output gap, and the renewable energy transition. The analysis uses a balanced annual panel dataset cove
content: This study examines the short-term dynamics of CO₂ emissions in advanced economies in relation to business cycles, energy intensity, the output gap, and the renewable energy transition. The analysis uses a balanced annual panel dataset covering 1991–2023, including G7 countries, Korea, Australia, Spain, the Netherlands, and Sweden. The study's main objective is to identify short-term emission determinants that are business cycle-sensitive and methodologically consistent, without relying on long-term equilibrium assumptions. Accordingly, because the panel lacks cointegration and shows mixed integration degrees, the analysis used short-term estimators: FE–Driscoll–Kraay, CCE-MG, and AMG. The findings show that per capita income growth and changes in energy intensity are key determinants of short-term emission growth. Increasing the share of renewable energy significantly reduces emissions growth. The output gap effect is asymmetric: expansion periods significantly affect emission dynamics, while contraction periods do not necessarily reduce emissions. The results show that emissions must be managed throughout business cycles and that renewable energy can play a stabilizing role in the short term.

title: Barsey Rhododendron Sanctuary: a model for preserving Himalayan biodiversity and nature-based tourism
source: Sibbaldia The International Journal Of Botanic Garden Horticulture
summary: Established in 1996 in response to substantial anthropogenic pressure, Barsey Rhododendron Sanctuary (Barsey) in Sikkim, India, serves as a model for biodiversity conservation. Spanning 104 km² in area and elevations ranging from 2,200 to 4
content: Established in 1996 in response to substantial anthropogenic pressure, Barsey Rhododendron Sanctuary (Barsey) in Sikkim, India, serves as a model for biodiversity conservation. Spanning 104 km² in area and elevations ranging from 2,200 to 4,100 m asl, Barsey protects a high diversity of Rhododendron, oaks and bamboos, as well as critical habitats for endangered fauna. Following the exclusion of grazing and the implementation of active community engagement through Eco-Development Committees, the sanctuary has demonstrated forest regeneration, increased carbon stocks, restored springs and a rise in ecotourism during Rhododendron flowering seasons. Here, we review the historical transformation of Barsey from a highly disturbed forest landscape to a recovering protected area, highlighting ecological outcomes, biodiversity gains and the role of local communities in conservation. We outline future research and conservation priorities, and ways to regulate tourism pressure, support off-season livelihoods and habitat restoration, and promote sustainable Rhododendron cultivation. Furthermore, we highlight the need to strengthen long-term ecological research and climate monitoring through community-led conservation initiatives.

title: Multiple environmental factors mediated-toxicity and mechanisms of environmentally relevant silver nanoparticles in Chlorella vulgaris
summary: The extensive application of silver nanoparticles (Ag NPs) has raised growing concerns regarding their potential ecological risks in aquatic environments. However, current studies remain largely on high dose exposure upon single factor, ove
content: The extensive application of silver nanoparticles (Ag NPs) has raised growing concerns regarding their potential ecological risks in aquatic environments. However, current studies remain largely on high dose exposure upon single factor, overlooking the complexity and heterogeneity of natural aquatic systems. This study investigated seven environmental factors on the response of Chlorella vulgaris ( C. vulgaris ) upon exposure of Ag NPs at environmentally relevant concentrations. The results showed that chloride ions (Cl - ), nitrogen and phosphorus nutrients, and light intensity are the dominant regulatory factors. Cl - exhibited the strongest mitigation, reducing C. vulgaris growth inhibition rate from 10.5% to −13.6% by promoting Ag NPs aggregation and reducing Ag bioavailability. Significant interactions were observed between dissolved organic maters (DOM) and pH, as well as phosphorus and temperature, which jointly regulated Ag NPs toxicity. Given the key role of DOM, the extracellular polymeric substances (EPS) secreted by C. vulgaris were further examined. EPS mitigates Ag NPs toxicity, by forming a protective layer, reducing direct contact between NPs and cells, and enhancing the Cl - buffering. Transmission electron microscopy showed that Cl - maintained cellular structural integrity, with EPS further enhancing organelle integrity. Metabolomic analysis indicated that Cl - significantly upregulated glutathione and α-linolenic acid metabolism, elevating reduced glutathione to 21.8-fold of the control (only 2.61-fold with EPS). Levels of 12-OPDA and 9-HpODE decreased significantly, while the milder reduction in 13-HOTrE with EPS indicated a buffering effect on membrane metabolic disorders. This study provides insights for elucidating the biological responses of Ag NPs in complex aquatic environments.

title: The current evidence of the performance enhancing effects of 20-hydroxyecdysone: A Scoping review with meta-analytical approach
summary: Purpose 20-Hydroxyecdysone (20E) has gained attention for its potential anabolic effects, with suggested efficacy comparable to prohibited agents. Consequently, the World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA) added 20E to its monitoring programme. 20E
content: Purpose 20-Hydroxyecdysone (20E) has gained attention for its potential anabolic effects, with suggested efficacy comparable to prohibited agents. Consequently, the World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA) added 20E to its monitoring programme. 20E is supposed to enhance protein synthesis and muscle hypertrophy; however, human evidence remains limited and often inaccessible due to Slavic and Turkic publications. Therefore, we aimed to evaluate the effects of 20E supplementation on strength performance and body composition in adults performing resistance training. Methods A systematic literature search was conducted in PubMed, Web of Science, SURF databases, and SportDiscus according to PRISMA guidelines. Eligible studies were randomized controlled trials administering a defined dose of 20E to participants performing resistance training and assessing strength performance (upper and/or lower body) and body composition (body weight, fat-free mass, fat mass). In vitro, animal, and observational studies were excluded . Results Four trials including 113 males and 37 females (mean age 33.4 ± 4 years) met inclusion criteria. Meta-analysis revealed a small but statistically significant effect of 20E on lower body strength (SMD: 0.39; 95% CI: 0.03–0.76; p = 0.03), with no significant effects on upper body strength or body composition. Only two studies verified the 20E content of the supplements, and one confirmed biological activity. Conclusion Evidence suggests a small beneficial effect of 20E on lower body strength. Findings are limited by the small number of studies and inadequate verification of supplement content and bioactivity. Future research should ensure accurate dosing and biological validation before conducting human intervention trials.

title: Biomethane from Wastewater Treatment Plants in the State of Minas Gerais: An Analysis of Production Potential and Associated Costs
summary: Biomethane is a renewable fuel obtained by upgrading biogas from anaerobic treatment of organic wastes and municipal wastewater. This study estimates the technical production potential and the levelized cost of biomethane (LCOB) for wastewa
content: Biomethane is a renewable fuel obtained by upgrading biogas from anaerobic treatment of organic wastes and municipal wastewater. This study estimates the technical production potential and the levelized cost of biomethane (LCOB) for wastewater treatment plants in Southern Minas Gerais, Brazil, and benchmarks scale effects with a reference set of larger Minas Gerais municipalities operating Upflow Anaerobic Sludge Blanket reactors. The assessment integrates population projections, wastewater generation and service coverage (collection/treatment), a COD-based methane balance with temperature correction, and capacity-parameterized CAPEX/OPEX equations to compute LCOB. In Southern Minas, LCOB spans US$0.49–12.72 per m 3 , Poços de Caldas at the lower bound (US$0.49) and Cambuí at the upper bound (US$12.72). In the expanded set, Uberaba and Contagem achieve US$0.26 per m 3 ; Uberaba is prioritized given its higher biomethane output. The total technical potential for Southern Minas is ≈1.19 million m 3 /year of useful biomethane (assuming 70% upgrading efficiency and 92% availability). A clear inverse relationship between methane flow (m 3 /h) and LCOB confirms economies of scale. Sensitivity tests (± 30% in OPEX, CAPEX, and discount rate) identify OPEX as the dominant driver of LCOB, followed by CAPEX and then the discount rate. The results support strategies focused on operational efficiency (energy management, predictive O&M), standardization/modularity, and scale-capturing arrangements (inter-municipal consortia, co-digestion, and integration with landfill gas). Transport and commercialization costs, excluded here, should be addressed in project-level evaluations.

title: Accelerating Phosphate Transport Across Membranes via Synergistic Chemical‐Electrochemical Carriers
summary: ABSTRACT Efficient phosphate recovery from phosphate‐containing wastewater presents a dual opportunity to mitigate environmental pollution and secure nutrient supply for agriculture. Among many recovery methods, electro‐membrane crystalliza
content: ABSTRACT Efficient phosphate recovery from phosphate‐containing wastewater presents a dual opportunity to mitigate environmental pollution and secure nutrient supply for agriculture. Among many recovery methods, electro‐membrane crystallization (e‐MC) is a promising strategy for sustainable phosphate recovery, yet the low phosphate throughput of conventional electro‐driven membranes constrains its efficacy. Here, we propose an ion carrier‐to‐carrier hopping transport principle and introduce a nanostructured electro‐driven carrier‐conducting membrane (e‐CCM) engineered with monodispersed electro‐ferrihydrite nanoparticles as a built‐in phosphate carrier. This membrane architecture establishes a coordination environment where ≡FeOH acts as transient phosphate binding sites, and the applied electric field promotes directional phosphate migration, thereby accelerating phosphate permeation. Operated at 5 mA cm −2 , the resulting e‐CCM membrane achieves a phosphate permeation rate of 0.92 mol m −2 h −1 and a recovery rate of 98.8%, outperforming state‐of‐the‐art ion exchange membranes. We further demonstrate scalability by integrating the e‐CCM membrane in e‐MC for processing simulated urine, achieving 93.6% phosphate recovery and the precipitation of high‐purity struvite. This work pioneers a hypothesis of carrier‐conducting construction that synergizes membrane electrochemical transport with chemical affinity, establishing a scalable and energy‐efficient pathway to close the phosphorus loop and advance circular resource economies.

title: Salt eustress modulates physiological responses and enhances yield, nutritional quality, and antioxidant capacity in sunflower microgreens
summary: Abstract Background Microgreens have gained attention as nutritious superfoods and as model systems for studying plant stress responses. Salt stress can elicit hormetic effects by enhancing plant growth and quality at low concentrations (eu
content: Abstract Background Microgreens have gained attention as nutritious superfoods and as model systems for studying plant stress responses. Salt stress can elicit hormetic effects by enhancing plant growth and quality at low concentrations (eustress) while inhibiting performance at higher levels (distress). Methods Sunflower ( Helianthus annuus L.) microgreens were hydroponically cultivated in a completely randomized design with three vessel replicates per treatment. Seedlings were grown for ten days using root-dipping technique in five NaCl concentrations (0–100 mM) under controlled natural environmental conditions. Growth parameters, physiological status, stress biomarkers, proximate composition, mineral content, fatty acid profile, and antioxidant capacity were assessed. Results Low stress induced by 25 mM NaCl increased shoot fresh yield (58.7%), shoot dry yield (55.4%), shoot length (48.3%), root length (25.7%), leaf area (81.4%), and specific leaf area (19.7%). Mild stress by 50 mM NaCl also improved growth, but its stimulatory effects were less pronounced. Conversely, moderate and severe stress levels (75 and 100 mM) significantly reduced these growth parameters. These responses were associated with modified physiological status indicated by photosynthesis and transpiration rates, chlorophyll content, relative water content, and water use efficiency. At 25 mM NaCl, proline content increased (5.7%), while catalase activity, lipid peroxidation, and H 2 O 2 content did not change significantly. Higher salt levels induced marked oxidative stress through elevated lipid peroxidation and H 2 O 2 accumulation. Nutritionally, 25 mM NaCl increased total carbohydrates (27.2%), total proteins (27.6%), Ca (11.9%), Mg (13.3%), Mn (14.3%), Zn (12.9%), and linoleic acid (5.0%). However, this low stress decreased ash content (–27.3%), total fats (–69.8%), K (–12.0%), Fe (–15.2%), palmitic acid (–9.7%), stearic acid (–12.2%), and oleic acid (–4.8%). Antioxidant profiling showed that 25 mM NaCl maximized total antioxidant activity (38.1%), DPPH-scavenging activity (6.0%), total phenols (8.8%), ascorbic acid (37.5%), and carotenoids (11.5%), while moderate and severe stress levels had opposite effects. Conclusion Low-dose salt eustress (25 mM NaCl) can be applied as a simple and cost-effective elicitor to improve growth, nutritional value, and antioxidant capacity of sunflower microgreens.

title: Microbial inoculant-mediated transformation of Jarava ichu biomass: effects on nutrient availability and heavy metal concentrations
summary: Introduction Jarava ichu is an abundant grass species in high-Andean ecosystems but remains underutilised because its slow natural decomposition limits its potential as an organic soil amendment. Its accumulation may also contribute to the
content: Introduction Jarava ichu is an abundant grass species in high-Andean ecosystems but remains underutilised because its slow natural decomposition limits its potential as an organic soil amendment. Its accumulation may also contribute to the retention of heavy metals in soils, potentially affecting soil quality and agricultural productivity. This study evaluated the effects of microbial inoculants on the physicochemical and mineral composition of J. ichu biomass and their potential to reduce heavy-metal concentrations. Methods A 2 × 2 × 2 factorial experiment was conducted under a randomised complete block design (RCBD), comprising eight treatments, including a non-inoculated control. The microbial inoculants evaluated were Beauveria bassiana , Trichoderma viride , and EM-Compost. After 180 days of incubation, pH, electrical conductivity (EC), organic matter (OM), macronutrients (N, P, K, Ca, and Mg), and heavy metals (Ni, Cr, and Pb) were determined. Treatment and interaction effects were evaluated to identify changes in biomass composition and contaminant concentrations. Results T. viride and EM-Compost significantly increased EC to 53.57 and 56.83 mS·m⁻¹, respectively, and enhanced macronutrient availability, particularly P (4,455.24 and 4,462.60 mg·kg⁻¹, respectively) and Mg (3,630.33 and 3,706.39 mg·kg⁻¹, respectively). T. viride reduced Ni and Cr concentrations by 15.53% and 19.75%, respectively, whereas EM-Compost reduced Pb concentration by 43.98%. Among the interaction effects, the combination of B. bassiana and EM-Compost produced the highest K concentration (2,659.45 mg·kg⁻¹). Discussion and conclusion Microbial inoculation promoted substantial changes in the chemical composition of J. ichu biomass after 180 days, particularly by increasing nutrient availability and reducing selected heavy-metal concentrations. T. viride and EM-Compost showed the greatest potential for enhancing nutrient release and reducing contaminants, suggesting that microbial treatment may improve the suitability of J. ichu biomass for subsequent valorisation as an organic soil amendment. Further studies should directly quantify decomposition rates, nutrient mineralisation, and the agronomic effects of the resulting biomass to confirm its potential for soil management.

title: A Review of Engineered Ferroelectric Materials: Synthesis Approaches, Physical Properties, and Technological Applications
summary: Ferroelectric materials are unique materials that possess spontaneous polarization, which can be reversed by the application of external electric field, making them versatile in the array of modern technologies. Their unique properties, suc
content: Ferroelectric materials are unique materials that possess spontaneous polarization, which can be reversed by the application of external electric field, making them versatile in the array of modern technologies. Their unique properties, such as high dielectric permittivity, piezoelectricity, pyroelectricity, and electro‐optic responses, make them applicable into the broad spectrum of applications such as sensors, nonvolatile memory devices, energy harvesting systems, actuators, microelectronic components. This review paper discusses the different ferroelectric materials and their synthesis techniques of the ferroelectric material which is used to determine the functionality and performance of these materials. Synthesis methods such as sol–gel processing, pulsed laser deposition, and chemical vapor deposition offer exact control over crystallinity, thickness of the film, and composition which influence material behavior. Furthermore, this review paper also discusses the applications of the ferroelectric materials and showcases the recent advancements that are shaping the future of ferroelectric technology. Ferroelectric materials ability to couple the electrical, mechanical, thermal, and optical responses makes them perfect fit for the multifunctional and adaptive devices. From miniaturized electronics to the adaptive devices, ferroelectric materials are at the cutting edge of the innovation in the field of clean energy.

title: Exploratory VOC profiling and chemometric differentiation of naturally and calcium carbide ripened bananas using GC-MS and electronic nose analysis
summary: Abstract In the world of rapid technological changes, artificially induced methods are often used to accelerate the ripening process particularly in banana fruits for more profit, despite quality and safety concerns. This study highlights n
content: Abstract In the world of rapid technological changes, artificially induced methods are often used to accelerate the ripening process particularly in banana fruits for more profit, despite quality and safety concerns. This study highlights noticeable differences in the chemical composition and quality of ‘Karpuravalli’ ,Pisang Awak type, ABB bananas that are ripened naturally and those subjected to calcium carbide during ripening. With the rationale of classifying naturally and calcium carbide treated banana fruits, this paper proposes a novel smart sensory method using headspace solid-phase micro extraction coupled with gas chromatography–mass spectrometry (GC-MS) technique. To implement our proposed method, an electronic nose equipped with TGS, MQ, and MP sensor arrays is developed to analyze and capture the distinctions existing in the chemical compositions of naturally and artificially ripened fruits using calcium carbide. Based on our empirical analysis, naturally ripened bananas exhibit higher concentrations of esters and long-chain hydrocarbon compounds resulting in their sweet and fruity aroma. Conversely, calcium carbide based artificially ripened fruits characterize higher amounts of acetylene (18.95%), ethylene (1.99%), causing physiological stress and harmful to health. Moreover, the classification is supported with a multivariate analysis using Principal Component Analysis (PCA), which accounted for 87.8% of the total variance, whereas further validation of chemical fingerprints of each ripening method is performed using partial least squares discriminant analysis. This proof-of-concept cross-validated exploratory chemometric analysis using modest sample size demonstrated moderate correlation between GC-MS-derived VOC profiles and E-nose sensor responses (R² = 0.80), indicating the feasibility of large-scale sensor-assisted differentiation of ripening methods under controlled experimental conditions.

title: FinTech-Driven Green Credit Markets
summary: Switching to a low-carbon economy will demand significant funding of environmentally-friendly investments. Nevertheless, commonly traditional financial systems are known to experience problems like high transaction costs, information asymme
content: Switching to a low-carbon economy will demand significant funding of environmentally-friendly investments. Nevertheless, commonly traditional financial systems are known to experience problems like high transaction costs, information asymmetry and less transparency which limits the efficient mobilization of green capital. The chapter discusses the potential of financial technology (FinTech) to revolutionize the green credit market and institutional channels of carbon reduction. The conceptual and analytical approach incorporating the results of the literature on sustainable finance, digital financial ecosystem, and climate policy, the chapter examines how digital lending platforms, blockchain-based verification, artificial intelligence-based credit evaluation, and data-driven environmental monitoring can improve the effectiveness and reliability of the green finance.

title: TURKISH ADAPTATION OF THE GREEN ORGANIZATIONAL IDENTIFICATION (GOI) SCALE: A VALIDITY AND RELIABILITY STUDY
summary: Background: Green organizational identification (GOI) reflects the extent to which employees identify with their organizations environmental values and goals and has become increasingly relevant in sustainability-oriented organizational beh
content: Background: Green organizational identification (GOI) reflects the extent to which employees identify with their organizations environmental values and goals and has become increasingly relevant in sustainability-oriented organizational behavior research. This study aimed to adapt the GOI Scale into Turkish and examine its psychometric properties in a sample of Turkish employees. Methods: Data were collected from 369 employees in Elazig, Turkiye. The scale was adapted using a forward-backward translation procedure, and linguistic and conceptual equivalence was evaluated through expert review. The factorial structure was examined using principal component analysis (PCA) and confirmatory factor analysis (CFA). Reliability was assessed using Cronbachs alpha, Spearman-Brown, Guttman split-half, and composite reliability coefficients; convergent validity was evaluated using average variance extracted (AVE). Nomological validity was examined through the relationships of GOI with psychological ownership and work alienation.

title: Remediation of sodium dodecyl sulfate-contaminated water using biochar derived from lemon peel and incorporated with calcium alginate beads
summary: Surfactants, a vital class of substances widely used in modern life, have detrimental effects on both aquatic life and human health. The current research work discusses a simple and environmentally sustainable method for removing sodium dod
content: Surfactants, a vital class of substances widely used in modern life, have detrimental effects on both aquatic life and human health. The current research work discusses a simple and environmentally sustainable method for removing sodium dodecyl sulphate (SDS), an anionic surfactant, from wastewater. For this purpose, lemon peel-derived biochar (LPBC) and calcium alginate (CA) were combined to get a novel composite adsorbent referred to as LPBCCA. Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy and scanning electron microscopy were used to characterize the LPBC, CA, and LPBCCA. The zero point charges of LPBC, CA, and LPBCCA were determined to be 4.3, 8.5, and 7.5, respectively. The batch adsorption experiment showed optimum pH values of 6, 8, and 7 for LPBC, CA, and LPBCCA, respectively. Under optimum conditions the maximum adsorption capacities were found to be 6.29, 1.86, and 42.77 mg/g for LPBC, CA, and LPBCCA, respectively. Isotherm studies suggested that adsorption of SDS on LPBC and CA followed the Temkin adsorption isotherm, while its adsorption on LPBCCA followed the Langmuir adsorption isotherm. The pseudo-second-order equation was more consistent with the adsorption kinetics results for LPBCCA and LPBC, indicating that chemical adsorption dominated the adsorption process. Adsorption on CA obeyed pseudo-first-order kinetics. Thermodynamic investigations revealed that sodium dodecyl sulfate adsorption on LPBC, CA, and LPBCCA was exothermic and spontaneous, with lower temperatures facilitating adsorption. Up to three cycles, LPBCCA has superior regeneration efficiency when compared to LPBC and CA. After three adsorption–desorption cycles, the regeneration analysis revealed that LPBCCA maintained 61% adsorption efficiency, suggesting moderate reusability and potential for recurrent application.

title: China’s diet urgently needs to establish a sustainable evaluation system to address critical challenges
summary: Assessing the diet’s sustainability is critical to advancing the Sustainable Development Goals. Dietary patterns have shifted from plant-based to animal-based, elevating health risks, intensifying environmental burdens, and necessitating sy
content: Assessing the diet’s sustainability is critical to advancing the Sustainable Development Goals. Dietary patterns have shifted from plant-based to animal-based, elevating health risks, intensifying environmental burdens, and necessitating systematic assessment and scientific responses. Current research on dietary sustainability is largely confined to national-level analyses, with few regional or provincial spatiotemporal studies. The study developed a tripartite framework integrating health, economic, and environmental indicators and applied it to 37 years of longitudinal data (1987–2023) to assess dietary sustainability at national, nine agricultural regions, and provincial scales. Nationally, the comprehensive sustainability of diets initially rose, then declined. While health and economic indicators improved, persistent environmental degradation emerged as the primary constraint. Across all nine agricultural regions, comprehensive sustainability increased, driven by gains in health and economic dimensions, despite universal declines in environmental sustainability. Provincial analysis revealed a shift in comprehensive sustainability from predominantly moderate—with some strong areas—to primarily strong, with scattered moderate areas. Notably, Tibet was the only province to register a decline. Health sustainability transitioned from a predominantly moderate pattern, marked by localized strengths and weaknesses, to an East‑West gradient, with higher levels in the East. Economic sustainability improved across all provinces, rising from weak‑to‑moderate levels to a very strong status. For environmental sustainability, all provinces except Gansu, Guizhou, Ningxia, and Shanxi showed a declining trend, with eastern regions of China experiencing pronounced deterioration. This spatial pattern shifted from a predominantly moderate baseline—encompassing both strong and weak areas—to one in which eastern sustainability falls below that in the west. Results revealed a structural contradiction from the imbalanced environmental, health, and economic dimensions’ synergies. Moving forward, coordinating the balanced development of environmental and other dimensions and reshaping the multidimensional balanced development path of the dietary system is essential.

title: Sewage sludge composted and bio-promoters enhance soil nutrient availability and initial development of Astronium fraxinifolium Schott
summary: Abstract This study evaluated the effects of sewage sludge composted (SSC, mixed with sugarcane bagasse at 1:1 ratio) and microbial biopromoters on soil fertility and early growth of Astronium fraxinifolium , a native tree with high recover
content: Abstract This study evaluated the effects of sewage sludge composted (SSC, mixed with sugarcane bagasse at 1:1 ratio) and microbial biopromoters on soil fertility and early growth of Astronium fraxinifolium , a native tree with high recovery potential in the Brazilian Cerrado. In a randomized block design (2 × 4 factorial), treatments consisted of two SSC levels (with and without 23 g pot⁻¹ of chemically characterized, environmentally safe compost) and four inoculation treatments (control; Bacillus subtilis - BS; Rhizophagus clarus - RhC; and BS + RhC) with five replicates in 6-L pots. After 150 days, growth, root morphology, gas exchange, and soil properties were evaluated. SSC improved soil fertility (reduced aluminum, increased P, sum of bases, base saturation, and essential micronutrients Fe, Mn, Zn) without inducing heavy metal toxicity, increasing plant height. The SSC + RhC interaction significantly promoted shoot and root biomass, stem diameter, and root surface area/volume. Seedling Quality Index (SQI) was highest under SSC + RhC and SSC + BS. Furthermore, SSC and inoculants significantly enhanced gas exchange parameters, translating into substantially higher photosynthetic performance. Overall, combining this specific SSC rate with biopromoters, particularly Rh. clarus , effectively improved soil chemical properties and seedling vigor. While limited to nursery conditions, these findings demonstrate that this approach successfully promotes high-quality seedlings, establishing a promising baseline for future long-term field validation and dose-response trials in degraded lands.

title: Surfacing the Economy: Representation, Valuation, and the Diverse Economies Iceberg
summary: ABSTRACT How are economic relations made apprehensible, valued, and consequential, and for whom? Work in critical human geography, economic sociology, and science and technology studies shows that “the economy” is not a pre‐given domain but
content: ABSTRACT How are economic relations made apprehensible, valued, and consequential, and for whom? Work in critical human geography, economic sociology, and science and technology studies shows that “the economy” is not a pre‐given domain but an effect of material, institutional, and representational practices that render some relations legible as economic while marginalizing others. Interventions such as the diverse economies framework have been central to this rethinking, particularly through the widely circulated “iceberg,” which foregrounds forms of labor, exchange, and interdependence marginalized in capitalocentric accounts. This paper uses the iceberg as a focal representational device through which to synthesize debates about economic representation and valuation. Building on diverse and community economies scholarship that has developed heterogeneous practices of inventory, measurement, recognition, and intervention, the paper develops surfacing as a comparative vocabulary for examining how actors, devices, and socio‐technical arrangements make economic relations apprehensible, valued, and consequential for particular audiences and institutional settings. Surfacing distinguishes recurring configurations of commensuration and incorporation, recognition without commensuration, and residualization and overflow without treating them as sequential stages or fixed outcomes. Reinterpreting the iceberg through this lens shows how economic boundaries and forms of value are produced, contested, and reorganized through differing relations among representation, valuation, recognition, and institutional uptake. The paper thereby offers a framework for comparing how economic plurality becomes consequential in different ways and settings.

title: Advances in sesame phyllody disease: Etiology, vector transmission, epidemiology, diagnosis and integrated management
summary: Sesame (Sesamum indicum L.) is an important oilseed crop whose productivity is significantly reduced by phyllody disease. Phytoplasmas present in the phloem tissue of the plant cause sesame witches'-broom disease. The abnormal development o
content: Sesame (Sesamum indicum L.) is an important oilseed crop whose productivity is significantly reduced by phyllody disease. Phytoplasmas present in the phloem tissue of the plant cause sesame witches'-broom disease. The abnormal development of a floral organ into a leaf-like structure (phyllody) and the development into green pigmentation in floral parts (virescence), resulting in sterility and reduced seed production. This disease is common in Africa and Asia and parts of Europe. Infection is mainly through insect vectors, especially the leafhoppers (Orosius albicinctus). Phyllody disease-associated phytoplasmas are of diverse ribosomal groups, with the 16SrII group associated with peanut witches'-broom highly prevalent. A fast and accurate diagnosis can be achieved using molecular diagnostics such as polymerase chain reaction (PCR). Phyllody negatively impacts many important agronomic traits of sesame, like plant height, number of capsules per plant and 1000 seed weight. Control of the disease involves some cultural practices (removal of symptomatic plants, use of certified disease-free seeds and change in planting date to avoid peak vector activity); limited chemical control by insecticides aimed only at the vector; and biological practices to improve the efficacy of natural vector antagonists. It seems that it is possible to develop sesame genotypes that are resistant or tolerant to phyllody, making it a sustainable management strategy. Yet, the polygenic nature of phyllody and the complicated nature of the resistance mechanisms have been an impediment. Further studies would be required to understand the ecology of the vectors and phytoplasma-host interaction and to facilitate the development of sesame varieties that have resistance or tolerance to disease. This review summarises current knowledge on the origin, transmission, epidemiology, symptomatology, diagnostics and management of sesame phyllody disease.

title: COUMARINS IN MEDICINAL CHEMISTRY: UNVEILING A PHARMACOLOGICALLY RICH SCAFFOLD
source: International Journal of Biology Pharmacy and Allied Sciences
summary: Coumarins are a class of compounds belonging to the benzopyrone family, consisting of a pyrone ring fused to a benzene ring.Benzopyrones are broadly divided into two categories: benzo-α-pyrones, which include coumarins, and benzo-γ-pyrones,
content: Coumarins are a class of compounds belonging to the benzopyrone family, consisting of a pyrone ring fused to a benzene ring.Benzopyrones are broadly divided into two categories: benzo-α-pyrones, which include coumarins, and benzo-γ-pyrones, which primarily encompass flavonoids.In nature, the three most commonly occurring coumarins are scopoletin, esculetin, and umbelliferone.Their biosynthesis involves precursor compounds such as p-coumaric acid, caffeic acid, and ferulic acid, which undergo a key transformation known as ortho-hydroxylation.Coumarins possess notable medicinal properties, making them valuable scaffolds for structural modification and drug development.They exhibit a wide range of biological activities, including antibacterial, anticancer, and anti-inflammatory effects, which has generated significant interest in exploring their therapeutic potential.

title: Interaction of water and supercritical carbon dioxide (ScCO2) with rock and joints
summary: Reservoir stimulation by hydraulic fracturing has become a superior technique by injecting high-pressure fluid into deep rock to initiate fractures, creating new fluid paths to improve oil and gas extraction. Water is the primary fluid used
content: Reservoir stimulation by hydraulic fracturing has become a superior technique by injecting high-pressure fluid into deep rock to initiate fractures, creating new fluid paths to improve oil and gas extraction. Water is the primary fluid used in hydraulic fracturing and has demonstrated advantages over the decades in enhancing reservoir permeability. While water is the most common fluid used in hydraulic fracturing, its use presents several significant limitations. Chief among them is the intense demand on local freshwater supplies, which can exacerbate water scarcity and compete with agricultural and municipal needs in arid regions. Furthermore, the flowback of contaminated water -containing dissolved salts, heavy metals, and naturally occurring radioactive materials -poses serious risks of soil and groundwater pollution if not properly managed. Finally, the disposal of this produced water through deep-well injection has been conclusively linked to induced seismicity, or human-caused earthquakes, creating geological instability. These limitations encourage the search for alternative fluids, such as supercritical carbon dioxide (ScCO 2 ). This paper employed a 2D fully coupled hydromechanical finite-discrete element method (FDEM) to study the performance of water and ScCO 2 in intact and jointed rocks. Important factors, including flow rate, in-situ stress magnitude, and fluid viscosity, are assessed for both the fluid and the results, and the results are compared with respect to the fluid-driven fracture pattern and breakdown pressure. The results confirm the extraordinary performance of ScCO 2 compared to water. ScCO 2 penetrates easily into rock grains and joints, easily dilates them, and generates fracture branching and long fractures. Moreover, breakdown pressures are lower than those of water, making it a preferred alternative to enhance permeability with less fluid energy.

title: Restoring Worker Subjectivity: Rethinking Dehumanization and the Crisis of HR
source: International Journal of Management and Humanities
summary: Organizational dehumanization and the growing fragmentation of the human resource (HR) function have been associated with employee stress, turnover, and declining organizational effectiveness. Although these issues have been widely discusse
content: Organizational dehumanization and the growing fragmentation of the human resource (HR) function have been associated with employee stress, turnover, and declining organizational effectiveness. Although these issues have been widely discussed, they are rarely examined within a unified theoretical perspective. This perspective paper aims to conceptually integrate these two organizational phenomena and examine how the recognition of worker subjectivity may contribute to improving employee well-being and organizational performance.
